objects.definition: typedef uint64_t nsSinceEpoch;
objects.description: Alias for a 64-bit unsigned integer representing nanoseconds since the UNIX epoch, or for monotonic tick values when used with monotonic APIs. Underlying type is uint64_t.

objects.definition: typedef uint64_t msSinceEpoch;
objects.description: Alias for a 64-bit unsigned integer representing milliseconds since the UNIX epoch, or for monotonic tick values when used with monotonic APIs. Underlying type is uint64_t.

objects.definition: typedef struct sThread* Thread;
objects.description: Opaque handle type for a thread object. It is a typedef to a pointer to an incomplete struct sThread, hiding implementation details. Used with the HAL thread API to create, start, and destroy threads.

objects.definition: typedef void* Semaphore;
objects.description: Opaque handle type for a semaphore object. It is a typedef to void*, with the concrete representation hidden. Used with the HAL semaphore API to create, wait, post, and destroy semaphores.

objects.definition: typedef void* (*ThreadExecutionFunction) (void*);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a thread entry function. The function takes a single void* parameter and returns a void* result (implementation-defined usage by the underlying platform).

objects.definition: typedef void* FileHandle;
objects.description: Opaque handle type representing an open file in the PAL filesystem HAL. It is a void* used as an identifier for file operations; its concrete structure is platform-specific and hidden.

objects.definition: typedef struct sDirectoryHandle* DirectoryHandle;
objects.description: Opaque handle to an opened directory in the PAL filesystem HAL. It is a pointer to an incomplete struct sDirectoryHandle; the actual definition is platform-specific and hidden.

objects.definition: typedef struct sEthernetSocket* EthernetSocket;
objects.description: Opaque handle to an Ethernet socket used by the PAL to send/receive raw Ethernet frames. The underlying struct sEthernetSocket is intentionally not defined in this header and must be treated as an opaque type.

objects.definition: typedef struct sEthernetHandleSet* EthernetHandleSet;
objects.description: Opaque reference to a set of Ethernet socket handles used for readiness waiting (select-like). The underlying struct sEthernetHandleSet is not defined here and remains opaque.

objects.definition: typedef struct sServerSocket* ServerSocket;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a TCP server socket instance used by the PAL socket abstraction. The underlying struct sServerSocket is intentionally hidden and defined elsewhere; only the opaque pointer is exposed here.

objects.definition: typedef struct sUdpSocket* UdpSocket;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a UDP socket instance (IPv4 or IPv6). The underlying struct sUdpSocket is opaque and defined elsewhere.

objects.definition: typedef struct sSocket* Socket;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a TCP client/connection socket (and in some APIs also used for accepted connections). The underlying struct sSocket is opaque and defined elsewhere.

objects.definition: typedef struct sHandleSet* HandleSet;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a set of socket handles used for readiness waiting (similar to fd_set for select). The actual struct sHandleSet is hidden.
Enumeration that represents the state of an asynchronous TCP connect operation: connecting, failed, or connected. This is a value type, not an opaque handle.

objects.definition: typedef struct sTLSConfiguration* TLSConfiguration;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a TLS configuration object encapsulating certificates, keys, trust store, cipher suites, protocol versions, and related validation/behavior settings. It is reference-like and must be created and destroyed via the provided API. Configuration becomes immutable once first used by the stack.
Enumeration of supported TLS/SSL protocol versions used for configuring min/max allowed protocol and for reporting connection version.
Severity levels for TLS security events delivered to the configured event handler.

objects.definition: typedef struct sTLSConnection* TLSConnection;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing a live TLS connection/channel, used for querying peer address, peer certificate, and negotiated TLS version in callbacks or connection context.

objects.definition: typedef void (*TLSConfiguration_EventHandler)(void* parameter, TLSEventLevel eventLevel, int eventCode, const char* message, TLSConnection con);
objects.description: Function pointer type for receiving TLS security events. Parameters: user parameter, event level, event code (see TLS_EVENT_CODE_* defines), message string, and the associated TLS connection (may be NULL depending on context).

Singly linked list node used by libIEC61850. Each node contains a generic data pointer and a pointer to the next node. The typedef LinkedList is a pointer to this node and is used both for the head of a list and for individual elements. Memory management of the data payload depends on which destroy function is used (shallow, deep via callback, or static).

objects.definition: typedef struct sLinkedList* LinkedList;
objects.description: Opaque handle (pointer) referring to a singly linked list node. Used as the public list/list-element type throughout the API. It aliases struct sLinkedList*.

objects.definition: typedef void (*LinkedListValueDeleteFunction) (void*);
objects.description: Function pointer type for per-element deleters used by LinkedList_destroyDeep. The function receives the void* data stored in a list node and should free or otherwise dispose it.

objects.definition: typedef struct sSNTPClient* SNTPClient;
objects.description: Opaque handle type for an SNTP client instance. The underlying struct sSNTPClient is intentionally not defined here, making it an incomplete type used as a handle for the SNTP client API. Lifetime is managed via SNTPClient_create and SNTPClient_destroy; start/stop control background operation.

objects.definition: typedef void (*SNTPClient_UserCallback)(void* parameter, bool isSynced);
objects.description: Function pointer type for user callbacks invoked by the SNTP client to report synchronization status changes. The callback receives a user-supplied parameter pointer and a boolean indicating whether the client is synchronized.
Holds Ethernet addressing and VLAN tagging parameters for IEC 61850 communications: VLAN priority, VLAN ID, APPID, and destination MAC address.

objects.description: Represents the Validity subfield within Quality. Constants (QUALITY_VALIDITY_*) define allowed values.
Double point status coded enum used by IEC 61850 to represent OFF/ON/intermediate/bad states.
UTC time (IEC 61850 Timestamp) stored as 8-byte array encoding seconds, fraction, and flags. Managed via Timestamp_* API for creation, conversion, and field manipulation.
Abstract base node for IEC 61850 data model hierarchy. Provides name, type, and intrusive linked-tree pointers (parent, sibling, firstChild).
Leaf node representing a data attribute with type, functional constraint, trigger options, MMS value binding, and optional short address. Supports arrays via elementCount/arrayIndex.
Composite model node corresponding to an IEC 61850 data object. May contain child DataObjects or DataAttributes and can represent array instances.
Model node for an IEC 61850 Logical Node (LN). Holds its name and children (data objects, control blocks, datasets, etc.) via the base tree pointers.
Model node for an IEC 61850 Logical Device (LD). Contains LNs as children and stores protocol-visible LD name (ldName) when functional naming is used.

Root of the IEC 61850 data model. Aggregates logical devices and top-level lists of datasets and control blocks. Usually generated by the model generator tool and optionally initialized via initializer().
Represents an IEC 61850 DataSet with a list of FCDAs (DataSetEntry). Linked via sibling for multiple datasets.

Configuration for IEC 61850 Reporting (BRCB/URCB). Stored under an LN, references a DataSet by name, carries trigger options, integrity period, buffering, and optional pre-configured client reservation.
SGCB representing setting group management parameters for an LN: active/edit group, confirmation state, reservation timer, etc.
GCB for GOOSE publishing. References dataset name, carries APPID, configuration revision, timing options, and a physical communication address.
Sampled Values control block defining SV stream parameters: ID, dataset, options, sampling mode/rate, config revision, destination address, unicast flag, and ASDU count.
LCB configuring logging for an LN. References dataset and target Log object, includes trigger and integrity options and flags for enable and reason codes.
Represents a Log (journal) object under a Logical Node; primarily a named target for LogControlBlocks.
Entry (FCDA or component) within a DataSet, referencing an element by LD name, variable and component names, optional index, and a bound MMS value. Entries are linked via sibling.

Enumeration of MMS value access/operation indications (result/status codes). Values cover successful operation and several error/exception conditions. Exact numeric values follow the listed order starting from 0 unless specified elsewhere.

Packed structure describing an MMS variable's type and, optionally, its name and detailed type-specific parameters. The 'type' field (MmsType, defined elsewhere) selects which member of the typeSpec union is valid. Supports arrays (with element count and element type spec), structures (with element count and array of element specs), integers (signed/unsigned bit width), floating point (exponent/format widths), bit strings, octet/visible/MMS strings, UTC time, and binary time. The ATTRIBUTE_PACKED indicates compiler-specific packing. Memory ownership: for composite types, elementTypeSpec or elements point to other MmsVariableSpecification instances managed by the creator. Destruction/management details are not provided in this header.

Opaque handle to a variable/type specification for MMS variables. Represents simple and complex MMS types (structures, arrays, named variables). This header only declares API functions operating on the type; the concrete definition is not provided here (forward/opaque type). Ownership/lifetime is managed by MmsVariableSpecification_destroy. Details of internal fields and construction are unknown from this header.

Opaque MMS value handle referenced by this API. Only referenced here; its full definition is not in this header. Used with MmsVariableSpecification_getChildValue and type checks. Construction, destruction, and internals are not defined here.

Opaque linked list handle used for returning structure element names. The list and its string elements are owned by the caller and can be released with LinkedList_destroy as noted. The concrete definition is not provided in this header.

Enumeration type identifying MMS base types. Only referenced here via MmsVariableSpecification_getType; not defined in this header. Pointer form given per requirements, but the enum definition is external.

The underlying struct sGooseReceiver is forward-declared and not defined in this header, indicating it is an internal, private type managed by the API. Instances are created and destroyed via the provided API functions. Details of the structure layout are unknown from this header.
Communication parameters for GOOSE/SMV Ethernet transport, including VLAN priority/ID, APPID, and destination MAC address (6 bytes). Used to configure on-wire fields for published GOOSE frames.

objects.definition: typedef struct sGoosePublisher* GoosePublisher;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a GOOSE publisher instance. Manages state (GoID, GoCbRef, stNum/sqNum, TAL, VLAN usage, etc.) and sends GOOSE frames over Ethernet or R-GOOSE via an RSession. Definition is not present in this header (opaque type).

objects.definition: typedef struct sSVSubscriber_ASDU* SVSubscriber_ASDU;

Instances are provided by the library during callbacks and are only valid for the duration of the SVUpdateListener call. Carries metadata (e.g., SmpCnt, SvID, DatSet, ConfRev, timing) and raw payload bytes from which typed values can be extracted via accessor functions.

objects.definition: typedef struct sSVSubscriber* SVSubscriber;
objects.description: Opaque handle type for an SV subscriber bound to a single SV data stream, identified by appID and optionally destination MAC address (and filtered also by svID at ASDU level). You attach an update listener to receive ASDUs for this stream.

objects.definition: typedef struct sSVReceiver* SVReceiver;
objects.description: Opaque handle type for an SV receiver responsible for capturing and dispatching SV Ethernet frames on a specific network interface or via an RSession. Manages one or more SVSubscriber objects and can operate threaded or threadless.

objects.definition: typedef void (*SVUpdateListener)(SVSubscriber subscriber, void* parameter, SVSubscriber_ASDU asdu);
objects.description: Function pointer type for the user-provided callback invoked for each received ASDU matching an SVSubscriber. The ASDU handle is only valid within the callback.

Structure holding communication parameters for SV/GOOSE frames, including VLAN priority and ID, application ID, and destination MAC address (6 bytes). Used to configure an SV publisher's VLAN tagging and destination address. Construction is by value allocation by the caller; lifetime is owned by the caller.

objects.definition: typedef struct sSVPublisher* SVPublisher;

objects.definition: typedef struct sSVPublisher_ASDU* SVPublisher_ASDU;

Represents the payload buffer and attributes (sample counter, timestamps, quality, etc.). Created via SVPublisher_addASDU and manipulated with SVPublisher_ASDU_* functions.

Start/stop networking and configure addresses, multicast, security, and keys via the RSession_* functions.
Enumeration of supported encryption algorithms for RSession security (protocol version 1). Used to configure encryption per session or per key.

functions.name: Hal_getTimeInMs
functions.description: Returns the current system wall-clock time as milliseconds since the UNIX epoch (1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC). Intended for general time-stamping where millisecond precision suffices. The return type msSinceEpoch is a uint64_t typedef.
requirements: No input arguments; no preconditions.
Caller should not assume monotonic behavior (value may jump due to system time adjustments).
Return value is a 64-bit millisecond count since UNIX epoch.

functions.name: Hal_getTimeInNs
functions.description: Returns the current system wall-clock time as nanoseconds since the UNIX epoch (1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC). Useful for high-resolution timestamps. The return type nsSinceEpoch is a uint64_t typedef.
requirements: No input arguments; no preconditions.
Caller should not assume monotonic behavior (value may jump due to system time adjustments).
Return value is a 64-bit nanosecond count since UNIX epoch.

functions.name: Hal_setTimeInNs
functions.description: Sets the system wall-clock time using a nanoseconds-since-UNIX-epoch value. Returns true on success, false otherwise. Use to adjust system time to a precise timestamp.
requirements: Argument nsTime must represent nanoseconds since the UNIX epoch (1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC).
Caller must check the boolean return value: true indicates the time was set; false indicates failure.
May require appropriate system privileges/permissions to set the system time (inferred from function purpose).
Should be called with a valid 64-bit timestamp value; behavior for out-of-range values is unspecified.

functions.name: Hal_getMonotonicTimeInMs
functions.description: Returns a monotonic time or system tick count in milliseconds. This value is intended for measuring intervals and is not affected by wall-clock adjustments. The return type msSinceEpoch is a uint64_t typedef; the absolute origin is unspecified and should be used only for relative timing.
requirements: No input arguments; no preconditions.
Caller should use this value only for relative measurements, not as a wall-clock timestamp.
Return value increases monotonically (subject to platform’s monotonic/tick semantics); not defined relative to UNIX epoch.

functions.name: Hal_getMonotonicTimeInNs
functions.description: Returns a monotonic time or system tick count in nanoseconds. Suitable for precise interval measurements and not subject to wall-clock changes. The return type nsSinceEpoch is a uint64_t typedef; the absolute epoch is unspecified and intended only for relative timing.
requirements: No input arguments; no preconditions.
Caller should use this value only for relative measurements, not as a wall-clock timestamp.
Return value increases monotonically (subject to platform’s monotonic/tick semantics); not defined relative to UNIX epoch.

functions.name: Thread_create
functions.signature: PAL_API Thread Thread_create(ThreadExecutionFunction function, void* parameter, bool autodestroy);
functions.description: Creates a new Thread object that will execute the provided ThreadExecutionFunction with the given parameter. If autodestroy is true, the thread object and its resources are automatically destroyed when the start routine returns; the handle must then be considered invalid. Typical usage: create, then call Thread_start to run the thread.
requirements: function must be a valid, callable function pointer of type void* (*)(void*).
parameter is passed verbatim to the start routine; if the routine dereferences it, it must remain valid for the duration of the routine (inferred from signature/usage).
If autodestroy is true, the Thread handle becomes invalid after the start routine finishes; the caller must not use or destroy it afterwards (stated in comment).
The returned Thread must be started explicitly with Thread_start to run (inferred from API design).

functions.name: Thread_start
functions.description: Starts execution of the given Thread by invoking its start function. The thread terminates when the start function returns.
requirements: thread must be a valid Thread created by Thread_create.
Should be called only on a thread that has not been started yet (inferred from typical threading semantics; behavior for repeated starts is unspecified).

functions.name: Thread_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a Thread and frees all related resources.
requirements: thread must be a valid Thread handle.

Do not call Thread_destroy on a thread created with autodestroy=true after its start function has finished, as the thread is automatically destroyed in that case (stated in Thread_create comment; inference on timing).
Behavior of destroying a running thread is unspecified; callers should ensure the thread is not needed anymore before destroying (unknown specifics).

functions.name: Thread_sleep
functions.description: Suspends execution of the calling thread for the specified number of milliseconds.
requirements: millies should be a non-negative integer (inferred from typical sleep semantics).
Function affects the calling thread only.

functions.name: Semaphore_create
functions.description: Creates a new semaphore with the given initial count value.
requirements: initialValue should be a non-negative integer (inferred from semaphore semantics).
Returned Semaphore must be destroyed with Semaphore_destroy when no longer needed.

functions.name: Semaphore_wait
functions.description: Blocks until the semaphore’s value is greater than zero, then decrements the value by one.
requirements: self must be a valid Semaphore returned by Semaphore_create.
This call may block indefinitely if the semaphore is not posted (no timeout is provided).

functions.name: Semaphore_post
functions.description: Increments (signals) the semaphore, potentially unblocking a waiting thread.
requirements: self must be a valid Semaphore returned by Semaphore_create.

functions.name: Semaphore_destroy
functions.description: Destroys the semaphore and frees associated resources.
requirements: self must be a valid Semaphore returned by Semaphore_create.
Destroying while other threads are blocked in Semaphore_wait has unspecified behavior (unknown; not documented).

functions.name: FileSystem_openFile
functions.signature: PAL_API FileHandle FileSystem_openFile(char* pathName, bool readWrite);
functions.description: Opens a file by full path and returns an opaque FileHandle for subsequent file operations. Pass readWrite=true for read/write access, false for read-only. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: pathName must be a valid, null-terminated string specifying the full path + filename.
Check the return value and do not use the handle if it is NULL (opening failed).
Use the returned handle only with FileSystem_* file functions and close it with FileSystem_closeFile when done.
If readWrite is true, the underlying file system must allow write access to the target path.

functions.name: FileSystem_readFile
functions.signature: PAL_API int FileSystem_readFile(FileHandle handle, uint8_t* buffer, int maxSize);
functions.description: Reads up to maxSize bytes from the current position of an open file into buffer, advancing the file position by the number of bytes read. Returns 0 on end-of-file.
requirements: handle must be a valid FileHandle returned by FileSystem_openFile and not yet closed.
buffer must be a valid pointer to writable memory of at least maxSize bytes.
maxSize must be >= 0; reading more than the buffer can hold is invalid.
Caller must handle a return value of 0 as end-of-file.
Do not call after FileSystem_closeFile on the handle.

functions.name: FileSystem_writeFile
functions.signature: PAL_API int FileSystem_writeFile(FileHandle handle, uint8_t* buffer, int size);
functions.description: Writes size bytes from buffer to an open file identified by handle. Returns the number of bytes actually written.
requirements: handle must be a valid FileHandle opened with write permissions (readWrite=true) and not yet closed.
buffer must point to at least size bytes of readable data.
size must be >= 0.
Check the return value; short writes are possible and indicate fewer bytes were written than requested.
Do not call after FileSystem_closeFile on the handle.

functions.name: FileSystem_closeFile
functions.description: Closes an open file associated with handle. After closing, the handle must not be used in further file operations.
requirements: handle must be a valid FileHandle obtained from FileSystem_openFile.
Do not reuse the handle after calling this function.

functions.name: FileSystem_getFileInfo
functions.signature: PAL_API bool FileSystem_getFileInfo(char* filename, uint32_t* fileSize, uint64_t* lastModificationTimestamp);
functions.description: Retrieves basic attributes of a file: its size in bytes and the timestamp of last modification in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Returns true if the file exists, false otherwise. If timestamps are not supported, lastModificationTimestamp is set to 0.
requirements: filename must be a valid, null-terminated string specifying the full path + filename.
fileSize must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the file size in bytes.
lastModificationTimestamp must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the last-modified timestamp (or 0 if not supported).
Caller must handle a return value of false to indicate the file does not exist.
Caller must handle lastModificationTimestamp == 0 as "not supported" by the platform.

functions.name: FileSystem_deleteFile
functions.description: Deletes the specified file by full path. Returns true on success, false on error.
requirements: filename must be a valid, null-terminated string specifying the full path + filename.
Caller must check the boolean return value to detect failure.

functions.name: FileSystem_renameFile
functions.signature: PAL_API bool FileSystem_renameFile(char* oldFilename, char* newFilename);
functions.description: Renames or moves a file from oldFilename to newFilename (full paths). Returns true on success, false on error.
requirements: oldFilename must be a valid, null-terminated string naming an existing file.
newFilename must be a valid, null-terminated string specifying the target path + filename.
Caller must check the boolean return value to detect failure.

functions.name: FileSystem_openDirectory
functions.description: Opens a directory for enumeration and returns an opaque DirectoryHandle for subsequent directory operations. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: directoryName must be a valid, null-terminated string specifying the directory path.
Check the return value and do not use the handle if it is NULL (opening failed).
Use the returned handle only with FileSystem_readDirectory and FileSystem_closeDirectory, and close it when done.

functions.name: FileSystem_readDirectory
functions.signature: PAL_API char* FileSystem_readDirectory(DirectoryHandle directory, bool* isDirectory);
functions.description: Reads the next entry from an open directory, returning the entry name. Sets *isDirectory to true if the entry itself is a directory. The returned name pointer remains valid only until the next FileSystem_readDirectory call for the same handle or until FileSystem_closeDirectory is called.
requirements: directory must be a valid DirectoryHandle returned by FileSystem_openDirectory and not yet closed.
isDirectory must be a non-NULL pointer to receive whether the entry is a directory.
Caller must copy the returned entry name if it needs to persist beyond the next read or directory close.
Do not call after FileSystem_closeDirectory on the handle.

functions.name: FileSystem_closeDirectory
functions.description: Closes an open directory associated with directory handle. After closing, the handle must not be used in further directory operations.
requirements: directory must be a valid DirectoryHandle obtained from FileSystem_openDirectory.
Do not reuse the handle after calling this function.

functions.name: EthernetHandleSet_new
functions.description: Create and return a new opaque EthernetHandleSet used to monitor multiple EthernetSocket instances for readability (similar to BSD select).

functions.name: EthernetHandleSet_addSocket
functions.description: Add an EthernetSocket to an existing EthernetHandleSet so it can be monitored by EthernetHandleSet_waitReady.
requirements: self must be a valid EthernetHandleSet previously created by EthernetHandleSet_new.
sock must be a valid EthernetSocket handle.

functions.name: EthernetHandleSet_removeSocket
functions.description: Remove a previously added EthernetSocket from an EthernetHandleSet.
requirements: self must be a valid EthernetHandleSet.
sock should be a socket previously added to self.

functions.name: EthernetHandleSet_waitReady
functions.description: Block up to timeoutMs milliseconds waiting for any socket in the set to have data available (BSD select-like). Returns the number of sockets with pending data, 0 on timeout, or -1 on socket error.
requirements: self must be a valid EthernetHandleSet containing zero or more sockets.
timeoutMs is specified in milliseconds.
Caller must check for a return value of -1 to detect a socket error and handle it appropriately.

functions.name: EthernetHandleSet_destroy
functions.description: Destroy an EthernetHandleSet and release its resources.
requirements: self must be a handle previously created by EthernetHandleSet_new.
Do not use self after this call.

functions.name: Ethernet_getInterfaceMACAddress
functions.signature: void Ethernet_getInterfaceMACAddress(const char* interfaceId, uint8_t* addr)
functions.description: Retrieve the MAC address of the given network interface and write the six address bytes to addr.
requirements: interfaceId must identify an existing Ethernet interface (e.g., OS-specific interface name).
addr must point to a buffer with space for at least 6 bytes to receive the MAC address.

functions.name: Ethernet_createSocket
functions.signature: EthernetSocket Ethernet_createSocket(const char* interfaceId, uint8_t* destAddress)
functions.description: Create an EthernetSocket bound to the specified interface and configured with a destination MAC address used for sending.
requirements: interfaceId must identify the Ethernet interface to use.
destAddress must point to a byte array containing the destination MAC address; this implies at least 6 bytes.

functions.name: Ethernet_destroySocket
functions.description: Close and destroy an EthernetSocket handle.
requirements: ethSocket must be a valid EthernetSocket returned by Ethernet_createSocket.
Do not use ethSocket after this call.

functions.name: Ethernet_sendPacket
functions.signature: void Ethernet_sendPacket(EthernetSocket ethSocket, uint8_t* buffer, int packetSize)
functions.description: Send a raw Ethernet packet via the given EthernetSocket. The packet data is taken from buffer with length packetSize. Exact framing requirements (e.g., inclusion of headers) are not specified in this header and may be implementation-specific.
requirements: ethSocket must be a valid EthernetSocket.
buffer must point to at least packetSize bytes of packet data.
packetSize must be non-negative and should reflect the actual number of bytes to send. Other size constraints (e.g., MTU) are not stated.

functions.name: Ethernet_setMode
functions.description: Configure the receive mode of an EthernetSocket (e.g., promiscuous, all-multicast, specific multicast, or host-only). If not implemented, the runtime must still be able to receive messages required by GOOSE/Sampled Values.
requirements: ethSocket must be a valid EthernetSocket.
mode must be one of the EthernetSocketMode enum values.

functions.name: Ethernet_addMulticastAddress
functions.description: Add a multicast MAC address to the EthernetSocket’s receive filter. Intended for use when the socket mode is ETHERNET_SOCKET_MODE_MULTICAST.
requirements: ethSocket must be a valid EthernetSocket.
multicastAddress must point to a buffer containing a multicast Ethernet MAC address with at least 6 bytes.
Should be used when the socket is configured with mode ETHERNET_SOCKET_MODE_MULTICAST.

functions.name: Ethernet_setProtocolFilter
functions.description: Set a protocol (EtherType) filter for the EthernetSocket to accept only frames with the specified EtherType. This is optional in implementations but can improve performance.
requirements: ethSocket must be a valid EthernetSocket.
etherType must be a valid 16-bit Ethernet EtherType value. No additional constraints are specified.

functions.name: Ethernet_receivePacket
functions.signature: int Ethernet_receivePacket(EthernetSocket ethSocket, uint8_t* buffer, int bufferSize)
functions.description: Non-blocking receive of a raw Ethernet packet from ethSocket. Copies up to bufferSize bytes into buffer and returns the size of the received message in bytes.
requirements: ethSocket must be a valid EthernetSocket.
buffer must point to writable memory with capacity of at least bufferSize bytes.
bufferSize specifies the maximum number of bytes to copy. Error/zero-length semantics beyond the stated return are not specified; caller should handle the returned size accordingly.

functions.name: Ethernet_isSupported
functions.description: Indicate whether the runtime environment provides support for direct (raw) Ethernet access.

functions.name: Handleset_new
functions.description: Create and return a new HandleSet used to monitor multiple sockets for readiness (similar to select). Intended as the starting point before adding sockets and waiting.
requirements: Must be called before using the HandleSet in other Handleset_* functions.
Returned HandleSet must later be destroyed with Handleset_destroy to free resources.

functions.name: Handleset_reset
functions.description: Reset a HandleSet instance so it can be reused for a new wait cycle.
requirements: self must be a valid HandleSet created by Handleset_new.
All sockets intended to be monitored after reset need to be (re)added with Handleset_addSocket if required by the implementation (not specified).

functions.name: Handleset_addSocket
functions.signature: PAL_API void Handleset_addSocket(HandleSet self, const Socket sock);
functions.description: Add a Socket to an existing HandleSet so it is included in subsequent readiness waits.
requirements: self must be a valid HandleSet instance.
sock must be a valid Socket handle.

functions.name: Handleset_removeSocket
functions.signature: void Handleset_removeSocket(HandleSet self, const Socket sock);
functions.description: Remove a previously added Socket from a HandleSet so it is no longer monitored.
requirements: self must be a valid HandleSet instance.
sock should refer to a Socket that may be present in the HandleSet (behavior if absent is unspecified).

functions.name: Handleset_waitReady
functions.signature: PAL_API int Handleset_waitReady(HandleSet self, unsigned int timeoutMs);
functions.description: Block until one or more sockets in the HandleSet become ready, or until timeout expires. Mirrors BSD select semantics.
requirements: self must be a valid HandleSet instance prepared with Handleset_addSocket.
timeoutMs is a timeout in milliseconds; function returns after this period if no data is pending.
Caller must handle return values: >0 = number of ready sockets; 0 = timeout/no data; -1 = socket error.

functions.name: Handleset_destroy
functions.description: Destroy a HandleSet and free associated resources.
requirements: self must be a HandleSet previously created by Handleset_new.
After destruction, self must not be used again.

functions.name: TcpServerSocket_create
functions.signature: PAL_API ServerSocket TcpServerSocket_create(const char* address, int port);
functions.description: Create a new TCP server socket bound to the given address and port for listening.
requirements: address is an IP address or hostname to listen on as a C string.
port is the TCP port to listen on.
Returned ServerSocket should later be destroyed with ServerSocket_destroy.

functions.name: UdpSocket_create
functions.description: Create a new IPv4 UDP socket instance.
requirements: Returned UdpSocket must be bound and configured as required before use (not specified).
Caller should destroy/close the socket via appropriate API when done (not specified in this header).

functions.name: UdpSocket_createIpV6
functions.description: Create a new IPv6 UDP socket instance.
requirements: Caller should use IPv6-compatible addresses with this socket.
Caller should destroy/close the socket via appropriate API when done (not specified in this header).

functions.name: UdpSocket_addGroupMembership
functions.signature: PAL_API bool UdpSocket_addGroupMembership(UdpSocket self, const char* multicastAddress);
functions.description: Join an IPv4 or IPv6 multicast group for the given UDP socket.
requirements: self must be a valid UdpSocket instance.
multicastAddress must be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 multicast address as a C string.
Caller must check the boolean return; false indicates failure and the membership was not added.

functions.name: UdpSocket_setMulticastTtl
functions.signature: PAL_API bool UdpSocket_setMulticastTtl(UdpSocket self, int ttl);
functions.description: Set the multicast TTL (hop limit) to control number of router hops for multicast packets sent by this UDP socket.
requirements: self must be a valid UdpSocket instance.
ttl is the number of hops; default is 1 (not routable).
Caller must check the boolean return value for success.

functions.name: UdpSocket_bind
functions.signature: PAL_API bool UdpSocket_bind(UdpSocket self, const char* address, int port);
functions.description: Bind the UDP socket to a local address and port.
requirements: self must be a valid UdpSocket instance.
address is a local IP address or hostname as a C string.
port is the local UDP port number.
Caller must check the boolean result; false indicates bind failure.

functions.name: UdpSocket_sendTo
functions.signature: PAL_API bool UdpSocket_sendTo(UdpSocket self, const char* address, int port, uint8_t* msg, int msgSize);
functions.description: Send a UDP datagram to the specified remote address and port.
requirements: self must be a valid UdpSocket instance.
address is the destination IP or hostname as a C string.
port is the destination UDP port.
msg points to the data buffer; msgSize is the number of bytes to send.
Caller must check the boolean result; false indicates send failure.

functions.name: UdpSocket_receiveFrom
functions.signature: PAL_API int UdpSocket_receiveFrom(UdpSocket self, char* address, int maxAddrSize, uint8_t* msg, int msgSize);
functions.description: Receive a UDP datagram from the socket, optionally returning the sender’s IP address string.
requirements: self must be a valid UdpSocket instance.
If address is provided (non-NULL), maxAddrSize must specify the size of the address buffer.
msg must point to a buffer at least msgSize bytes long; msgSize is the maximum number of bytes to read.
Caller must handle return values: >=0 = number of bytes received; -1 = error.

functions.name: ServerSocket_listen
functions.description: Put the server socket into listening state to accept incoming connections.
requirements: self must be a valid ServerSocket returned by TcpServerSocket_create.
Should be called before ServerSocket_accept (ordering implied by semantics).

functions.name: ServerSocket_accept
functions.description: Accept a pending incoming TCP connection in a non-blocking manner, returning a new connection Socket or NULL if none is pending.
requirements: self must be a valid listening ServerSocket.
Caller must handle NULL return when no connection is available.
Returned Socket must be destroyed with Socket_destroy when no longer needed.

functions.name: Socket_activateTcpKeepAlive
functions.signature: PAL_API void Socket_activateTcpKeepAlive(Socket self, int idleTime, int interval, int count);
functions.description: Enable TCP keepalive on the given socket and set keepalive parameters: idle time, probe interval, and probe count.
requirements: self must be a valid Socket.
idleTime is seconds between last received message and first keepalive probe.
interval is seconds between keepalive probes when no ACK received.
count is number of missing keepalive ACKs before the socket is considered dead.

functions.name: ServerSocket_setBacklog
functions.signature: PAL_API void ServerSocket_setBacklog(ServerSocket self, int backlog);
functions.description: Set the maximum number of pending connections in the accept queue for the server socket (optional implementation).
requirements: self must be a valid ServerSocket.
backlog is the maximum queue length for pending connections.

functions.name: ServerSocket_destroy
functions.description: Destroy a server socket, closing and freeing all resources associated with it.
requirements: self must be a ServerSocket previously created by TcpServerSocket_create.
After destruction, the handle must not be used again.

functions.name: TcpSocket_create
functions.description: Create a new TCP client socket instance.
requirements: Returned Socket should be connected (e.g., via Socket_connect or Socket_connectAsync) before read/write.
Socket must be destroyed with Socket_destroy when done.

functions.name: Socket_setConnectTimeout
functions.signature: PAL_API void Socket_setConnectTimeout(Socket self, uint32_t timeoutInMs);
functions.description: Set the timeout (in milliseconds) used when establishing a new TCP connection for this socket.
requirements: self must be a valid client Socket.
timeoutInMs is the connect timeout in milliseconds.

functions.name: Socket_bind
functions.signature: PAL_API bool Socket_bind(Socket self, const char* srcAddress, int srcPort);
functions.description: Bind a TCP socket to a specific local source address and port before connecting.
requirements: self must be a valid client Socket.
srcAddress is the local IP address or hostname as a C string.
srcPort is the local TCP port; when < 1 the OS chooses the port.
Caller must check the boolean result; if false, do not use the socket (per note).

functions.name: Socket_connect
functions.signature: PAL_API bool Socket_connect(Socket self, const char* address, int port);
functions.description: Synchronously connect the TCP client socket to a server at the specified address and port.
requirements: self must be a valid client Socket.
address is an IP address or hostname as a C string.
port is the server TCP port.
Caller must check the boolean result to confirm the connection was established.

functions.name: Socket_connectAsync
functions.signature: PAL_API bool Socket_connectAsync(Socket self, const char* address, int port);
functions.description: Initiate a non-blocking TCP connection attempt to the specified server address and port.
requirements: self must be a valid client Socket.
address is an IP address or hostname as a C string.
port is the server TCP port.
Caller should poll using Socket_checkAsyncConnectState to determine completion state.
Caller must check the boolean return; false indicates the async connect could not be started.

functions.name: Socket_checkAsyncConnectState
functions.description: Check the state of a previously initiated asynchronous connection attempt, returning CONNECTING, FAILED, or CONNECTED.
requirements: self must be a valid client Socket on which Socket_connectAsync was called.
Caller must handle all possible returned states: SOCKET_STATE_CONNECTING, SOCKET_STATE_FAILED, SOCKET_STATE_CONNECTED.

functions.name: Socket_read
functions.signature: PAL_API int Socket_read(Socket self, uint8_t* buf, int size);
functions.description: Non-blocking read from a socket into the provided buffer. Returns immediately if no data is available.
requirements: self must be a valid Socket (client, connection, or server socket instance as stated).
buf must point to a buffer of at least size bytes.
Caller must handle return values: >0 = bytes read; 0 = no data available; -1 = error.

functions.name: Socket_write
functions.signature: PAL_API int Socket_write(Socket self, uint8_t* buf, int size);
functions.description: Send data through the socket from the provided buffer.
requirements: self must be a valid Socket (client, connection, or server).
buf points to the data to send; size is the number of bytes to transmit.
Caller must handle return values: >=0 = bytes transmitted; -1 = error.

functions.name: Socket_getLocalAddress
functions.description: Return the local socket address as a null-terminated string. Specific format and ownership are not documented.
requirements: self must be a valid Socket.
Memory ownership/lifetime of the returned string is unknown; caller should consult implementation (unknown).

functions.name: Socket_getPeerAddress
functions.description: Return the peer address (IP and port) as a null-terminated string, fields separated by ':'.
requirements: self must be a valid Socket.
Format: IP:port; for IPv6, details are not specified here (see Static variant for bracket note).
Memory ownership/lifetime of the returned string is not specified (unknown).

functions.name: Socket_getPeerAddressStatic
functions.signature: PAL_API char* Socket_getPeerAddressStatic(Socket self, char* peerAddressString);
functions.description: Write the peer address (IP and port) into the provided buffer as a string; for IPv6, the IP portion is enclosed in square brackets.
requirements: self must be a valid Socket.
peerAddressString must have space for at least 60 characters (as stated).
Returns the same string pointer; caller must use the provided buffer for storage.

functions.name: Socket_destroy
functions.description: Close any established connection and free all resources associated with the Socket.
requirements: self must be a Socket previously created by TcpSocket_create or returned by ServerSocket_accept.
After destruction, the handle must not be used again.

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_create
functions.description: Creates a new TLSConfiguration object used to hold TLS configuration data (protocol versions, ciphers, credentials, trust, etc.). Use the returned handle with the various TLSConfiguration_* setter functions before using it in any TLS connection.
requirements: Must be called before using the configuration in any TLS session; after first use, the configuration is no longer changeable (per header warning).
Caller must check the returned handle for NULL if the implementation can fail (unknown from header).

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_setClientMode
functions.description: Marks the TLS configuration for client mode. Intended to be called by the stack automatically when appropriate.
requirements: self must be a valid, initialized TLSConfiguration.
Should be called before the configuration is first used, as configuration cannot be changed after first use.

functions.name: TLSConfigVersion_toString
functions.description: Converts a TLSConfigVersion enum value to a human-readable, null-terminated string for logging or UI.
requirements: version must be a valid TLSConfigVersion enumerator.
Returned pointer refers to immutable storage; do not modify. Lifetime/ownership are not documented (likely static).

functions.name: TLSConnection_getPeerAddress
functions.description: Returns the remote peer's address and port as a null-terminated string for a TLS connection. If peerAddrBuf is NULL, the function may allocate and return a new buffer; otherwise it writes into the provided buffer.
requirements: self must be a valid, active TLSConnection.
If peerAddrBuf is not NULL, it must point to a buffer capable of holding at least 60 characters.
If peerAddrBuf is NULL, the function allocates the buffer; ownership/lifetime and who frees it are not documented (unknown).
Returned pointer must be checked for NULL to detect failure (not explicitly documented).

functions.name: TLSConnection_getPeerCertificate
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the peer's TLS certificate buffer and writes its size (bytes) to certSize.
requirements: self must be a valid, active TLSConnection with a completed handshake.
certSize must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the certificate size.
Returned pointer refers to certificate data managed by the TLS stack; lifetime/ownership not documented (unknown).
Caller should not modify the returned buffer unless documentation explicitly allows it (unknown).

functions.name: TLSConnection_getTLSVersion
functions.description: Returns the negotiated TLS protocol version used by the connection.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConnection (preferably post-handshake).

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_setEventHandler
functions.signature: void TLSConfiguration_setEventHandler(TLSConfiguration self, TLSConfiguration_EventHandler handler, void* parameter);
functions.description: Registers a security event callback to receive TLS-related informational, warning, or incident events for connections using this configuration. The parameter is passed to the callback on each event.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
handler may be NULL to clear the handler (not documented; behavior unknown).
Callback must match: void (*TLSConfiguration_EventHandler)(void* parameter, TLSEventLevel eventLevel, int eventCode, const char* message, TLSConnection con).
Must be set before first use of the configuration if it should apply to all sessions (configuration becomes immutable after first use).
Callback implementation must be re-entrant or thread-safe if events can be raised concurrently (not documented; concurrency model unknown).

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_enableSessionResumption
functions.description: Enables or disables TLS session resumption for sessions using this configuration. Default is enabled. Implemented via session IDs or session tickets depending on TLS version.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_setSessionResumptionInterval
functions.description: Sets the maximum lifetime (in seconds) of cached TLS sessions used for resumption.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
intervalInSeconds should be a non-negative integer (not explicitly documented; exact bounds unknown).
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_setChainValidation
functions.description: Enables or disables validation of the certificate trust chain when authenticating peers. Enabled by default.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_setTimeValidation
functions.description: Enables or disables checking of certificate and CRL validity periods. Enabled by default.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_setAllowOnlyKnownCertificates
functions.description: If enabled, only previously configured/known peer certificates are accepted; unknown certificates are rejected even if signed by a trusted CA.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_setOwnCertificate
functions.signature: bool TLSConfiguration_setOwnCertificate(TLSConfiguration self, uint8_t* certificate, int certLen);
functions.description: Sets the local identity certificate from a memory buffer.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
certificate must be a non-NULL pointer to the certificate bytes.
certLen must be the size in bytes of certificate and should be > 0.
Certificate must be in a format recognized by the TLS backend; function returns false on unknown/unsupported format.
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).
Caller must check the boolean return value and handle failure.

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_setOwnCertificateFromFile
functions.description: Sets the local identity certificate from a certificate file.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
filename must be a non-NULL, readable path to a certificate file in a supported format.
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).
Caller must check the boolean return value and handle failure.

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_setOwnKey
functions.signature: bool TLSConfiguration_setOwnKey(TLSConfiguration self, uint8_t* key, int keyLen, const char* keyPassword);
functions.description: Sets the local private key from a memory buffer. keyPassword may be NULL if the key is not password-protected.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
key must be a non-NULL pointer to the key bytes.
keyLen must be the size in bytes of key and should be > 0.
keyPassword may be NULL for unprotected keys; otherwise must point to a null-terminated password string.
Key must be in a format recognized by the TLS backend; function returns false on unknown/unsupported format.
The key must match the configured certificate for successful use (not explicitly enforced here).
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).
Caller must check the boolean return value and handle failure.

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_setOwnKeyFromFile
functions.signature: bool TLSConfiguration_setOwnKeyFromFile(TLSConfiguration self, const char* filename, const char* keyPassword);
functions.description: Sets the local private key from a key file. keyPassword may be NULL if the key is not password-protected.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
filename must be a non-NULL, readable path to a key file in a supported format.
keyPassword may be NULL for unprotected keys; otherwise must point to a null-terminated password string.
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).
Caller must check the boolean return value and handle failure.

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_addAllowedCertificate
functions.signature: bool TLSConfiguration_addAllowedCertificate(TLSConfiguration self, uint8_t* certificate, int certLen);
functions.description: Adds a peer certificate (from memory) to the allowlist of certificates accepted when 'allow only known certificates' is enabled.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
certificate must be non-NULL and certLen should be > 0.
Certificate must be in a supported/recognized format; function returns false otherwise.
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).
Caller must check the boolean return value and handle failure.

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_addAllowedCertificateFromFile
functions.description: Adds a peer certificate (from file) to the allowlist of certificates accepted when 'allow only known certificates' is enabled.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
filename must be a non-NULL, readable path to a certificate file in a supported format.
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).
Caller must check the boolean return value and handle failure.

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_addCACertificate
functions.signature: bool TLSConfiguration_addCACertificate(TLSConfiguration self, uint8_t* certificate, int certLen);
functions.description: Adds a CA certificate (from memory) used to validate peer certificate chains.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
certificate must be non-NULL and certLen should be > 0.
Certificate must be in a supported/recognized format; function returns false otherwise.
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).
Caller must check the boolean return value and handle failure.

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_addCACertificateFromFile
functions.description: Adds a CA certificate (from file) used to validate peer certificate chains.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
filename must be a non-NULL, readable path to a certificate file in a supported format.
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).
Caller must check the boolean return value and handle failure.

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_setRenegotiationTime
functions.description: Sets the TLS session renegotiation timeout in milliseconds. When the timeout elapses, renegotiation must occur.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
timeInMs should be a non-negative integer (not explicitly documented; exact bounds unknown).
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_setMinTlsVersion
functions.description: Sets the minimal allowed TLS protocol version for sessions using this configuration.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
version must be a valid TLSConfigVersion enumerator.
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_setMaxTlsVersion
functions.description: Sets the maximal allowed TLS protocol version for sessions using this configuration.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
version must be a valid TLSConfigVersion enumerator.
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_addCRL
functions.signature: bool TLSConfiguration_addCRL(TLSConfiguration self, uint8_t* crl, int crlLen);
functions.description: Adds a Certificate Revocation List (CRL) from a memory buffer to be used during certificate validation.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
crl must be non-NULL and crlLen should be > 0.
CRL must be in a supported/recognized format; function returns false otherwise.
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).
Caller must check the boolean return value and handle failure.

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_addCRLFromFile
functions.description: Adds a Certificate Revocation List (CRL) from a file to be used during certificate validation.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
filename must be a non-NULL, readable path to a CRL file in a supported format.
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).
Caller must check the boolean return value and handle failure.

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_resetCRL
functions.description: Removes any CRL currently configured for use in certificate validation.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_addCipherSuite
functions.description: Adds an allowed TLS cipher suite (specified by its IANA cipher suite ID) to the configuration's allowlist.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
ciphersuite must be an integer IANA cipher suite ID; support depends on the TLS backend (unknown).
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_clearCipherSuiteList
functions.description: Clears the configured list of allowed cipher suites, typically to start with an empty set before adding specific suites.
requirements: self must be a valid TLSConfiguration.
Call before the configuration is first used (immutable after first use).

functions.name: TLSConfiguration_destroy
functions.description: Releases all resources associated with the TLSConfiguration. The handle must not be used after destruction.
requirements: self may be NULL (behavior not documented; typically a no-op if NULL but unknown).
Must not be called while in use by active connections (not documented; safe usage implies destroying only when no sessions reference it).
Do not use the object after calling this function (explicit note).

functions.name: LinkedList_create
functions.description: Creates and returns a new LinkedList instance (an empty list/head element). Intended as the constructor/initializer for this list type.
requirements: Caller must store and later destroy the returned list with one of the destroy functions (LinkedList_destroy, LinkedList_destroyDeep, or LinkedList_destroyStatic).
Behavior on allocation failure is unknown (return value may be NULL; not documented).

functions.name: LinkedList_destroy
functions.description: Destroys the LinkedList and frees all internal list nodes and their data by calling free on each data element. Use this when all stored elements are simple objects allocated with malloc (e.g., dynamically allocated strings) that can be freed with free.
requirements: self must be a valid LinkedList previously created/initialized and not already destroyed.
All data pointers stored in the list must be safely deallocatable with free; otherwise this call may mismanage memory or crash.
After this call, the LinkedList instance and its elements must not be used.

functions.name: LinkedList_destroyDeep
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void LinkedList_destroyDeep(LinkedList self, LinkedListValueDeleteFunction valueDeleteFunction);
functions.description: Destroys the LinkedList and frees all internal list nodes. For each data element, the provided valueDeleteFunction is called, allowing the caller to properly free/cleanup each stored object.
requirements: self must be a valid LinkedList previously created/initialized and not already destroyed.
valueDeleteFunction must be a valid function pointer; it will be called once for each data element in the list and must correctly dispose of the element data.
valueDeleteFunction must tolerate being called with the exact pointers stored in the list.
After this call, the LinkedList instance and its elements must not be used.

functions.name: LinkedList_destroyStatic
functions.description: Destroys the LinkedList and frees internal list nodes but does not free the data elements. Use this when the stored data is statically allocated or managed elsewhere.
requirements: self must be a valid LinkedList previously created/initialized and not already destroyed.
Caller remains responsible for any memory or resources owned by the data elements.
After this call, the LinkedList instance and its elements must not be used.

functions.name: LinkedList_add
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void LinkedList_add(LinkedList self, void* data);
functions.description: Appends a new element containing data to the end of the list.
requirements: self must be a valid LinkedList.
No guarantees are stated about accepting NULL for data (behavior unknown).

functions.name: LinkedList_contains
functions.signature: LIB61850_API bool LinkedList_contains(LinkedList self, void* data);
functions.description: Checks whether the specified data pointer is contained in the list and returns true if present, false otherwise.
requirements: self must be a valid LinkedList.
Equality semantics are not documented; based on typical patterns, comparison is likely pointer equality (unknown).

functions.name: LinkedList_remove
functions.signature: LIB61850_API bool LinkedList_remove(LinkedList self, void* data);
functions.description: Removes the element containing the specified data from the list. Returns true if an element was removed, false otherwise. Whether the data itself is freed is not documented.
requirements: self must be a valid LinkedList.
Data matching semantics are not documented; likely pointer equality (unknown).
Whether this function frees the removed element’s data is not stated; callers should assume data is not freed unless using a destroy function (unknown).

functions.name: LinkedList_get
functions.signature: LIB61850_API LinkedList LinkedList_get(LinkedList self, int index);
functions.description: Returns the list element at the specified zero-based index.
requirements: self must be a valid LinkedList.
index should be >= 0 and less than the current list size; behavior for out-of-range indices is not documented (may return NULL; unknown).

functions.name: LinkedList_getNext
functions.description: Returns the next element in the list (iterator-style). Pass a list element to get its successor.
requirements: self must be a valid list element (non-NULL).
If self is the last element, the return value is not documented (likely NULL; unknown).

functions.name: LinkedList_getLastElement
functions.description: Returns the last element of the list.
requirements: self must be a valid LinkedList.
Return value when the list is empty is not documented (likely NULL; unknown).

functions.name: LinkedList_insertAfter
functions.signature: LIB61850_API LinkedList LinkedList_insertAfter(LinkedList listElement, void* data);
functions.description: Inserts a new element containing data directly after listElement and returns the newly created element.
requirements: listElement must be a valid element belonging to a LinkedList.
No guarantees are stated about accepting NULL for data (behavior unknown).

functions.name: LinkedList_size
functions.description: Returns the number of data elements stored in the list.
requirements: self must be a valid LinkedList.

functions.name: LinkedList_getData
functions.description: Returns the data pointer stored in the given list element.
requirements: self must be a valid list element (non-NULL).

functions.name: LinkedList_printStringList
functions.description: Prints the list assuming it contains C strings. Useful for debugging string lists.
requirements: self must be a valid LinkedList.

functions.name: SNTPClient_create
functions.description: Creates a new SNTP client instance and returns an opaque handle (SNTPClient) used with the other SNTP client APIs. Typically called once per client you intend to configure and run.
requirements: Must be called before using the handle with any other SNTPClient_* function.
Caller must check the returned handle for NULL to detect allocation or initialization failure (failure mode not documented; inferred).
The returned handle must later be released with SNTPClient_destroy to avoid resource leaks.

functions.name: SNTPClient_setLocalAddress
functions.signature: void SNTPClient_setLocalAddress(SNTPClient self, const char* localAddress);
functions.description: Sets the local IP address the SNTP client should bind to for UDP communication. Use before starting the client to control the outgoing interface/bind address.
requirements: self must be a valid SNTPClient created by SNTPClient_create and not yet destroyed.
localAddress must be a valid, null-terminated string representing a local IP address (IPv4/IPv6 as supported by the build; exact formats not documented).
Should be called before SNTPClient_start for the setting to take effect (inferred from typical behavior).

functions.name: SNTPClient_setLocalPort

requirements: self must be a valid SNTPClient created by SNTPClient_create and not yet destroyed.
udpPort should be a valid UDP port number in the range 0–65535 (inferred from UDP semantics).
Should be called before SNTPClient_start for the setting to take effect (inferred).

functions.name: SNTPClient_getHandleSet
functions.description: Returns the HandleSet associated with the SNTP client for integration with the library’s socket/event handling (from hal_socket.h). Typically used to add client sockets to a select/poll loop managed by the application.
requirements: self must be a valid SNTPClient created by SNTPClient_create and not yet destroyed.
Caller should treat the returned HandleSet as owned by the SNTP client; do not free or modify beyond operations intended by the HAL (exact ownership not documented; inferred).
May need to be queried before driving an event loop or when integrating with external select/poll (usage details not documented; some behavior inferred).

functions.name: SNTPClient_addServer
functions.signature: void SNTPClient_addServer(SNTPClient self, const char* serverAddr, int serverPort);
functions.description: Adds an SNTP/NTP server endpoint the client may query for time synchronization. Multiple calls likely add multiple servers (not explicitly documented).
requirements: self must be a valid SNTPClient created by SNTPClient_create and not yet destroyed.
serverAddr must be a valid, null-terminated hostname or IP address string.
serverPort should be a valid UDP port number in the range 0–65535 (inferred).
Should be called before SNTPClient_start to ensure servers are used when synchronization begins (inferred).

functions.name: SNTPClient_setPollInterval
functions.description: Configures the polling interval (in seconds) at which the client contacts configured SNTP servers to maintain synchronization.
requirements: self must be a valid SNTPClient created by SNTPClient_create and not yet destroyed.
intervalInSeconds should be greater than 0 to enable periodic polling (not documented; inferred from semantics).
Should be configured before SNTPClient_start for predictable behavior (inferred).

functions.name: SNTPClient_setUserCallback
functions.signature: void SNTPClient_setUserCallback(SNTPClient self, SNTPClient_UserCallback callback, void* parameter);
functions.description: Registers a user callback that will be invoked to signal synchronization status changes. The callback receives the provided user parameter and a boolean indicating whether the client is synchronized.
requirements: self must be a valid SNTPClient created by SNTPClient_create and not yet destroyed.
callback may be NULL to clear the callback (not documented; unknown—behavior if NULL is set is unspecified).
The callback must be reentrant and safe to call from an internal networking/event context; exact calling thread and timing are not documented (unknown).
The pointer parameter is opaque and passed through unmodified; the caller must ensure it remains valid for as long as the callback may be invoked.

functions.name: SNTPClient_isSynchronized
functions.description: Returns whether the SNTP client currently considers its time synchronized with a configured server.
requirements: self must be a valid SNTPClient created by SNTPClient_create and not yet destroyed.
May be called whether the client is started or not; exact semantics before start are not documented (unknown).

functions.name: SNTPClient_start
functions.description: Starts the SNTP client’s internal processing (e.g., socket setup, periodic polling). After starting, the client begins contacting servers and may invoke the user callback.
requirements: self must be a valid SNTPClient created by SNTPClient_create and not yet destroyed.
Should only be called after configuring local address/port, servers, and poll interval as needed (inferred).
Should not be called multiple times without an intervening SNTPClient_stop (inferred; repeated starts may be undefined).

functions.name: SNTPClient_stop
functions.description: Stops the SNTP client’s internal processing and network activity without destroying the instance. Can be started again later.
requirements: self must be a valid SNTPClient created by SNTPClient_create and not yet destroyed.
Should be called to cease activity before SNTPClient_destroy (inferred).
Should not be called if the client was not started; behavior in that case is not documented (unknown).

functions.name: SNTPClient_destroy
functions.description: Releases all resources associated with the SNTP client handle. After this call, the handle must not be used.
requirements: self must be a valid SNTPClient created by SNTPClient_create; passing NULL is typically a no-op but not documented (unknown).
self must not be used after SNTPClient_destroy returns.
Recommended to stop the client with SNTPClient_stop before destroying to ensure clean shutdown (inferred).
Call exactly once per created client to avoid leaks or double-free (inferred).

functions.name: FunctionalConstraint_toString

functions.name: Quality_getValidity

functions.name: Quality_unsetFlag

flag should be a bit mask composed of QUALITY_DETAIL_* and/or other QUALITY_* flag constants.

functions.name: Quality_isFlagSet

requirements: self must be a non-NULL pointer to a Quality value to be checked.

requirements: If mmsValue is non-NULL, it must be an MmsValue suitable to hold a Dbpos bit string; otherwise pass NULL to request allocation by the function.
dbpos must be a valid Dbpos enumeration value.
Returns an MmsValue* or NULL on error (error conditions not detailed here).
