handler should be non-NULL.

functions.name: MmsConnection_getFileDirectory
functions.signature: LIB61850_API bool MmsConnection_getFileDirectory(MmsConnection self, MmsError* mmsError, const char* fileSpecification, const char* continueAfter, MmsFileDirectoryHandler handler, void* handlerParameter);
functions.description: Retrieve file directory entries for a server directory (blocking). Calls handler once per entry and once with filename=NULL at the end. Returns true if more data is available server-side (more follows).
requirements: self must be a valid MmsConnection.
mmsError must be a valid pointer.
fileSpecification may be NULL to browse root; otherwise a directory/file pattern.
continueAfter is a continuation point: first entry after provided filename; may be NULL for first segment.
handler must be non-NULL; handlerParameter is passed to it.

functions.name: MmsConnection_getFileDirectoryAsync
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void MmsConnection_getFileDirectoryAsync(MmsConnection self, uint32_t* usedInvokeId, MmsError* mmsError, const char* fileSpecification, const char* continueAfter, MmsConnection_FileDirectoryHandler handler, void* parameter);
functions.description: Asynchronously get file directory entries; entries and continuation/moreFollows are delivered via handler.
requirements: self must be a valid MmsConnection.
usedInvokeId and mmsError must be valid pointers.
fileSpecification may be NULL for root; continueAfter may be NULL for first call.
handler must be non-NULL.

functions.name: MmsJournalEntry_destroy
functions.description: Destroy (free) a single MmsJournalEntry including attached MmsJournalVariable list. Intended for use with LinkedList_destroyDeep.
requirements: self must be a valid MmsJournalEntry or NULL.
When destroying lists returned by readJournal functions, use LinkedList_destroyDeep with this as deleter.

functions.name: MmsJournalEntry_getEntryID
functions.description: Get the entryID (MMS_OCTET_STRING) value of a journal entry.
requirements: self must be a valid MmsJournalEntry.
Returned MmsValue belongs to the entry; lifetime/ownership as per library conventions (not specified here).

functions.name: MmsJournalEntry_getOccurenceTime
functions.description: Get the occurrence time (MMS_BINARY_TIME) of a journal entry.
requirements: self must be a valid MmsJournalEntry.
Returned MmsValue belongs to the entry; ownership per library conventions.

functions.name: MmsJournalEntry_getJournalVariables
functions.description: Get the list of MmsJournalVariable entries associated with a journal entry.
requirements: self must be a valid MmsJournalEntry.
Returned LinkedList contains MmsJournalVariable objects owned by the entry.

functions.name: MmsJournalVariable_getTag
functions.description: Get the tag (name) of a journal variable.
requirements: self must be a valid MmsJournalVariable.
Returned pointer is valid while the MmsJournalVariable exists.

functions.name: MmsJournalVariable_getValue
functions.description: Get the MmsValue of a journal variable.
requirements: self must be a valid MmsJournalVariable.
Returned MmsValue is owned by the journal variable per library conventions.

functions.name: MmsConnection_readJournalTimeRange
functions.signature: LIB61850_API LinkedList MmsConnection_readJournalTimeRange(MmsConnection self, MmsError* mmsError, const char* domainId, const char* itemId, MmsValue* startTime, MmsValue* endTime, bool* moreFollows);
functions.description: Read journal entries within a time range (blocking). Returns a LinkedList of MmsJournalEntry objects and indicates if more data follows.
requirements: self must be a valid MmsConnection.
mmsError must be a valid pointer.
domainId and itemId identify the journal.
startTime and endTime are MmsValue* time specifications of appropriate types.
moreFollows may be NULL or a valid pointer to receive continuation flag.
Caller must destroy returned list with LinkedList_destroyDeep using MmsJournalEntry_destroy.

functions.name: MmsConnection_readJournalTimeRangeAsync
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void MmsConnection_readJournalTimeRangeAsync(MmsConnection self, uint32_t* usedInvokeId, MmsError* mmsError, const char* domainId, const char* itemId, MmsValue* startTime, MmsValue* endTime, MmsConnection_ReadJournalHandler handler, void* parameter);
functions.description: Asynchronously read journal entries within a time range; entries and moreFollows delivered via handler.
requirements: self must be a valid MmsConnection.
usedInvokeId and mmsError must be valid pointers.
domainId/itemId identify the journal; startTime/endTime must be valid MmsValue time specs.
handler must be non-NULL.

functions.name: MmsConnection_readJournalStartAfter
functions.signature: LIB61850_API LinkedList MmsConnection_readJournalStartAfter(MmsConnection self, MmsError* mmsError, const char* domainId, const char* itemId, MmsValue* timeSpecification, MmsValue* entrySpecification, bool* moreFollows);
functions.description: Read journal entries starting after a given time and entry specification (blocking). Returns a LinkedList of MmsJournalEntry and indicates if more follows.
requirements: self must be a valid MmsConnection.
mmsError must be a valid pointer.
domainId/itemId identify the journal.
timeSpecification and entrySpecification are MmsValue* of appropriate types for journal selection.
moreFollows may be NULL or a valid pointer to receive continuation flag.
Caller must destroy returned list with LinkedList_destroyDeep using MmsJournalEntry_destroy.

functions.name: MmsConnection_readJournalStartAfterAsync
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void MmsConnection_readJournalStartAfterAsync(MmsConnection self, uint32_t* usedInvokeId, MmsError* mmsError, const char* domainId, const char* itemId, MmsValue* timeSpecification, MmsValue* entrySpecification, MmsConnection_ReadJournalHandler handler, void* parameter);
functions.description: Asynchronously read journal entries starting after given specifications; entries and moreFollows delivered via handler.
requirements: self must be a valid MmsConnection.
usedInvokeId and mmsError must be valid pointers.
domainId/itemId identify the journal; timeSpecification/entrySpecification must be valid MmsValue objects.
handler must be non-NULL.

functions.name: MmsServer_installFileAccessHandler
functions.signature: void MmsServer_installFileAccessHandler(MmsServer self, MmsFileAccessHandler handler, void* parameter)
functions.description: Registers a callback to be invoked whenever a client requests an MMS file service operation, allowing the application to monitor and control file access. The handler receives the connection context, the requested file service type, and relevant filenames, and must decide whether to allow or deny the request by returning an appropriate MmsError. Typical use is to enforce access control and logging for MMS file services on the server.
requirements: self must be a valid, initialized MmsServer instance.

handler must be a function of type MmsFileAccessHandler: MmsError (*)(void* parameter, MmsServerConnection connection, MmsFileServiceType service, const char* localFilename, const char* otherFilename).

The installed handler must return MMS_ERROR_NONE to accept a request, or an appropriate MMS_ERROR_* code (e.g., MMS_ERROR_FILE_FILE_ACCESS_DENIED) to reject it, as stated in the MmsFileAccessHandler documentation.
parameter is an opaque user-provided pointer passed through to the handler; acceptable values are not specified (may be implementation-defined/unknown).

functions.name: AcseAuthenticationParameter_create
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new ACSE authentication parameter object used to configure authentication (password, certificate, or TLS) for ACSE. Typically called before setting mechanism and credentials, then passed to ISO/MMS connection configuration.
requirements: Must be called before using the returned object in other AcseAuthenticationParameter_* functions.
Caller must eventually destroy the returned object with AcseAuthenticationParameter_destroy to avoid leaks.

functions.name: AcseAuthenticationParameter_destroy
functions.description: Releases resources associated with an ACSE authentication parameter object created by AcseAuthenticationParameter_create.
requirements: self must be a valid AcseAuthenticationParameter previously created by AcseAuthenticationParameter_create.
self must not be used after this call.

functions.name: AcseAuthenticationParameter_setAuthMechanism
functions.description: Sets the ACSE authentication mechanism (none, password, certificate, or TLS) to be used by the authentication parameter object.
requirements: self must be a valid AcseAuthenticationParameter.
mechanism must be one of: ACSE_AUTH_NONE, ACSE_AUTH_PASSWORD, ACSE_AUTH_CERTIFICATE, ACSE_AUTH_TLS.

functions.name: AcseAuthenticationParameter_getAuthMechanism
functions.description: Returns the currently selected authentication mechanism for the given ACSE authentication parameter object.
requirements: self must be a valid AcseAuthenticationParameter.

functions.name: AcseAuthenticationParameter_setPassword
functions.description: Sets the ACSE password to be used when the mechanism is ACSE_AUTH_PASSWORD. The implementation stores the password and tracks its length.
requirements: self must be a valid AcseAuthenticationParameter.
password must be a valid C string (null-terminated).
If ACSE_AUTH_PASSWORD is intended, set the mechanism accordingly via AcseAuthenticationParameter_setAuthMechanism.

functions.name: AcseAuthenticationParameter_getPassword
functions.description: Returns the stored password string from the ACSE authentication parameter object when password authentication is used. Returns a pointer to internally held data.
requirements: self must be a valid AcseAuthenticationParameter.
Returned pointer is owned by the library; do not free or modify it.

functions.name: AcseAuthenticationParameter_getPasswordLength
functions.description: Returns the length (in bytes) of the stored ACSE password.
requirements: self must be a valid AcseAuthenticationParameter.

functions.name: IsoApplicationReference_getAeQualifier
functions.description: Returns the AE-Qualifier from an ISO Application Reference. Used during ACSE authentication callbacks and connection setup.
requirements: self must be a valid IsoApplicationReference.

functions.name: IsoApplicationReference_getApTitle
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the AP-Title (as an ITU Object Identifier) from an ISO Application Reference.
requirements: self must point to a valid IsoApplicationReference.
Returned pointer refers to data owned by the IsoApplicationReference; do not free or modify it.

functions.name: ItuObjectIdentifier_getArcCount
functions.description: Returns the number of arcs (subidentifiers) contained in the given ITU Object Identifier.
requirements: self must be a valid ItuObjectIdentifier.

functions.name: ItuObjectIdentifier_getArc
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the array of arcs (subidentifiers) of the given ITU Object Identifier as 16-bit values.
requirements: self must be a valid ItuObjectIdentifier.
Returned pointer is to memory owned by the object; do not free or modify it.
The valid range for indexing the array is 0 .. ItuObjectIdentifier_getArcCount(self)-1.

functions.name: IsoConnectionParameters_create
functions.description: Creates a new ISO connection parameters object used to configure host/port, AP-Title/AE-Qualifier, and lower layer selectors for an MMS/IEC 61850 client connection. Intended primarily for library internal use.
requirements: Caller must destroy the returned object with IsoConnectionParameters_destroy when no longer needed.

functions.name: IsoConnectionParameters_destroy
functions.description: Destroys an ISO connection parameters object previously created by IsoConnectionParameters_create. Intended primarily for library internal use.
requirements: self must be a valid IsoConnectionParameters.
Do not use self after destruction.

functions.name: IsoConnectionParameters_setTlsConfiguration
functions.description: Associates a TLS configuration with the ISO connection parameters for TLS-secured connections. Available when the library is built with TLS support.
requirements: self must be a valid IsoConnectionParameters.
tlsConfig must be a valid TLSConfiguration initialized per tls_config.h.
Only effective if the library was compiled with CONFIG_MMS_SUPPORT_TLS == 1.

functions.name: IsoConnectionParameters_setAcseAuthenticationParameter
functions.description: Sets the ACSE authentication parameter on the ISO connection. This activates authentication using the provided parameters.
requirements: self must be a valid IsoConnectionParameters.
acseAuthParameter must be a valid AcseAuthenticationParameter configured with the desired mechanism and credentials.

functions.name: IsoConnectionParameters_setTcpParameters
functions.signature: void IsoConnectionParameters_setTcpParameters(IsoConnectionParameters self, const char* hostname, int tcpPort)
functions.description: Sets the remote TCP/IP endpoint (hostname/IP and port) for the ISO/MMS connection. Marked as for library internal use.
requirements: self must be a valid IsoConnectionParameters.
hostname must be a valid null-terminated string designating the remote host or IP address.
tcpPort must be a valid TCP port number (typically 0–65535).

functions.name: IsoConnectionParameters_setLocalTcpParameters
functions.signature: void IsoConnectionParameters_setLocalTcpParameters(IsoConnectionParameters self, const char* localIpAddress, int localTcpPort)
functions.description: Sets the local TCP bind address and port to use for the connection. Marked as for library internal use.
requirements: self must be a valid IsoConnectionParameters.
localIpAddress must be a valid null-terminated string designating the local IP address or hostname.
localTcpPort must be a valid TCP port number (typically 0–65535).

functions.name: IsoConnectionParameters_setRemoteApTitle
functions.signature: void IsoConnectionParameters_setRemoteApTitle(IsoConnectionParameters self, const char* apTitle, int aeQualifier)
functions.description: Sets the remote AP-Title (OID string) and AE-Qualifier used in the ACSE association. Calling is optional; if apTitle is NULL the AP-Title and AE-Qualifier will not be transmitted (required by some servers).
requirements: self must be a valid IsoConnectionParameters.
apTitle may be NULL to suppress sending AP-Title and AE-Qualifier; if non-NULL it must be a valid null-terminated OID string.
aeQualifier is an integer; its interpretation follows ACSE/ISO conventions.

functions.name: IsoConnectionParameters_setRemoteAddresses
functions.signature: void IsoConnectionParameters_setRemoteAddresses(IsoConnectionParameters self, PSelector pSelector, SSelector sSelector, TSelector tSelector)
functions.description: Sets the remote lower-layer addresses: P-Selector (presentation), S-Selector (session), and T-Selector (transport). Calling is optional; defaults are used otherwise.
requirements: self must be a valid IsoConnectionParameters.
For PSelector.size and SSelector.size: 0..16 where 0 means selector is not present (per struct documentation).
For TSelector.size: 0..4 where 0 means selector is not present.
Selector value arrays must contain the intended bytes up to the given size.

functions.name: IsoConnectionParameters_setLocalApTitle
functions.signature: void IsoConnectionParameters_setLocalApTitle(IsoConnectionParameters self, const char* apTitle, int aeQualifier)
functions.description: Sets the local AP-Title (OID string) and AE-Qualifier. Calling is optional; if apTitle is NULL the AP-Title and AE-Qualifier will not be transmitted.
requirements: self must be a valid IsoConnectionParameters.
apTitle may be NULL to suppress sending AP-Title and AE-Qualifier; if non-NULL it must be a valid null-terminated OID string.
aeQualifier is an integer per ACSE/ISO conventions.

functions.name: IsoConnectionParameters_setLocalAddresses
functions.signature: void IsoConnectionParameters_setLocalAddresses(IsoConnectionParameters self, PSelector pSelector, SSelector sSelector, TSelector tSelector)
functions.description: Sets the local lower-layer addresses: P-Selector, S-Selector, and T-Selector. Calling is optional; defaults are used otherwise.
requirements: self must be a valid IsoConnectionParameters.
For PSelector.size and SSelector.size: 0..16 where 0 means selector is not present (per struct documentation).
For TSelector.size: 0..4 where 0 means selector is not present.
Selector value arrays must contain the intended bytes up to the given size.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_create
functions.signature: LIB61850_API GooseSubscriber GooseSubscriber_create(char* goCbRef, MmsValue* dataSetValues);
functions.description: Create a new GOOSE subscriber bound to a specific GOOSE Control Block reference (GoCB). If dataSetValues is provided, received dataset elements are written into this MMS_ARRAY; otherwise it will be created on first matching message. Intended usage: construct once per desired GoCB, optionally with a pre-created MmsValue array (e.g., obtained via IedConnection_getDataSet).
requirements: goCbRef must be a valid, null-terminated C-string in MMS notation for the desired GoCB (e.g., "simpleIOGenericIO/LLN0$GO$gcbEvents").
If dataSetValues is non-NULL, it must be an MmsValue of type MMS_ARRAY whose element types match the dataset elements of the publisher’s GOOSE message (typically created by IedConnection_getDataSet).
If dataSetValues is NULL, the subscriber will create the MmsValue upon receipt of the first appropriate GOOSE message.
Caller owns the returned GooseSubscriber and must destroy it with GooseSubscriber_destroy unless it is managed by a GooseReceiver.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_getGoId
functions.description: Return the GoId value from the last received GOOSE message for this subscriber.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.
A GOOSE message must have been received to return a meaningful value; otherwise the returned pointer content may be unspecified by this header.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_getGoCbRef
functions.description: Return the GOOSE Control Block reference (GoCB ref) from the last received GOOSE message for this subscriber.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.
A GOOSE message must have been received to return a meaningful value; otherwise the returned pointer content may be unspecified by this header.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_getDataSet
functions.description: Return the datSet (dataset reference) string from the last received GOOSE message for this subscriber.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.
A GOOSE message must have been received to return a meaningful value; otherwise the returned pointer content may be unspecified by this header.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_setDstMac
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void GooseSubscriber_setDstMac(GooseSubscriber self, uint8_t dstMac[6]);
functions.description: Configure a destination MAC address filter for this subscriber. When set, only GOOSE frames with the matching destination MAC are processed.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.
dstMac must point to an array of at least 6 bytes containing the desired destination MAC address.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_setAppId
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void GooseSubscriber_setAppId(GooseSubscriber self, uint16_t appId);
functions.description: Configure an APPID filter for this subscriber. When set, only GOOSE frames with the matching APPID are processed.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_isValid
functions.description: Report whether the subscriber’s state is valid: TimeAllowedToLive has not expired and received messages have correct state and sequence IDs.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_getParseError
functions.description: Return the parse error code describing the message parse problem of the last received message, useful when the subscriber is invalid.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_destroy
functions.description: Destroy and free a GooseSubscriber instance. Do not call this if the instance has been added to a GooseReceiver; it will be destroyed by GooseReceiver_destroy instead.
requirements: self must be a GooseSubscriber instance not currently owned/managed by a GooseReceiver.
If the subscriber was added to a GooseReceiver, it must be removed (or let GooseReceiver_destroy handle destruction) before calling this function.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_setListener
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void GooseSubscriber_setListener(GooseSubscriber self, GooseListener listener, void* parameter);
functions.description: Register a callback invoked when a GOOSE message is received. The provided parameter is passed through to the callback.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.
listener must be a valid function pointer or NULL to clear the listener (behavior when NULL is not explicitly documented).

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_getAppId
functions.description: Return the APPID value of the last received GOOSE message.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_getSrcMac
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void GooseSubscriber_getSrcMac(GooseSubscriber self, uint8_t* buffer);
functions.description: Copy the source MAC address of the last received GOOSE message into the provided buffer.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.
buffer must point to writable memory of at least 6 bytes.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_getDstMac
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void GooseSubscriber_getDstMac(GooseSubscriber self, uint8_t* buffer);
functions.description: Copy the destination MAC address of the last received GOOSE message into the provided buffer.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.
buffer must point to writable memory of at least 6 bytes.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_getStNum
functions.description: Return the state number (stNum) from the last received GOOSE message. stNum increments when dataset values change due to a valid trigger.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_getSqNum
functions.description: Return the sequence number (sqNum) from the last received GOOSE message. It increments for consecutive messages without state change and resets when stNum increases.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_isTest
functions.description: Return the test flag from the last received GOOSE message. Note: Per the standard, messages with test=TRUE must be ignored.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.
Caller should ignore messages when this function returns true to remain standard compliant.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_getConfRev
functions.description: Return the confRev value from the last received GOOSE message; returns 0 if not present in the message.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_needsCommission
functions.description: Return the ndsCom (needs commission) flag from the last received GOOSE message. Note: Per the standard, messages with ndsCom=TRUE must be ignored.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.
Caller should ignore messages when this function returns true to remain standard compliant.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_getTimeAllowedToLive
functions.description: Return the TimeAllowedToLive (TAL) of the last received GOOSE message in milliseconds.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_getTimestamp
functions.description: Return the timestamp of the last received GOOSE message in milliseconds since the Unix epoch (1970-01-01 UTC).
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_getDataSetValues
functions.description: Return the MmsValue array holding the dataset values from the last received GOOSE message. Note: To prevent data corruption when the receiver runs in a separate thread, use this object only inside the listener callback.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.
If the GOOSE receiver runs in a separate thread, the returned MmsValue pointer should be used only inside the callback that delivered the message to avoid data corruption.
Caller should treat the returned pointer as owned by the subscriber; do not free it.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_isVlanSet
functions.description: Return whether VLAN tagging information is set for the last received GOOSE message.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_getVlanId
functions.description: Return the VLAN ID of the last received GOOSE message.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.
Meaningful value is available only if GooseSubscriber_isVlanSet(self) returns true.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_getVlanPrio
functions.description: Return the VLAN priority of the last received GOOSE message.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.
Meaningful value is available only if GooseSubscriber_isVlanSet(self) returns true.

functions.name: GooseSubscriber_setObserver
functions.description: Configure the subscriber to observe (listen to) any received GOOSE message, not only those matching preconfigured filters. When enabled, the subscriber can also access goCbRef, goId, and datSet values from received messages.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseSubscriber instance.

functions.name: GooseReceiver_create
functions.description: Create a new GooseReceiver instance to handle incoming GOOSE messages on a network interface. Use with threaded (start/stop) or non-threaded (startThreadless/tick/handleMessage) operation.
requirements: Must be called before using any other GooseReceiver_* functions on the instance.
Returned GooseReceiver must be destroyed with GooseReceiver_destroy to free resources.
The returned instance is not running until GooseReceiver_start or GooseReceiver_startThreadless is called.

functions.name: GooseReceiver_createEx
functions.description: Create a new GooseReceiver using a caller-provided buffer for Ethernet messages, or NULL if using GooseReceiver_handleMessage. Enables avoiding internal buffer allocation.
requirements: If buffer is non-NULL, it must point to valid writable memory for use by the receiver; required size is not specified in this header (unknown).
If you plan to use GooseReceiver_handleMessage (manual message injection), pass buffer == NULL as documented.
Returned GooseReceiver must be destroyed with GooseReceiver_destroy to free resources.
Do not free or reuse the provided buffer for other purposes while the receiver may access it (lifetime must cover receiver usage).

functions.name: GooseReceiver_createRemote
functions.description: Create a new R-GOOSE (remote GOOSE) receiver bound to the provided remote session protocol instance.
requirements: session must be a valid, initialized RSession object suitable for R-GOOSE use (details not specified in this header).
Returned GooseReceiver must be destroyed with GooseReceiver_destroy to free resources.
Receiver is not running until GooseReceiver_start or GooseReceiver_startThreadless is called.

functions.name: GooseReceiver_setInterfaceId
functions.description: Set the network interface identifier (e.g., OS-specific interface name) for the GooseReceiver to receive GOOSE messages on.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseReceiver created by a create function and not yet destroyed.
interfaceId must be a valid, null-terminated string naming an Ethernet interface recognizable by the underlying platform (exact format is platform-specific, unknown here).
Should be called before GooseReceiver_start (implied by typical usage; not strictly stated).
Do not call concurrently with GooseReceiver_start/stop or while the receiver thread is running (implied thread-safety concern; not explicitly stated).

functions.name: GooseReceiver_getInterfaceId
functions.description: Return the Ethernet interface ID string configured for the GooseReceiver.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseReceiver created by a create function and not destroyed.
Returned pointer refers to an internal string; lifetime/ownership unspecified (do not modify; copying is safest).

functions.name: GooseReceiver_addSubscriber
functions.description: Attach a GooseSubscriber to this receiver so it will be notified/updated for matching GOOSE messages.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseReceiver and not destroyed.
subscriber must be a valid, initialized GooseSubscriber.
Must NOT be called while the receiver is running (after GooseReceiver_start) as explicitly documented.
Call before GooseReceiver_start or after GooseReceiver_stop completes.

functions.name: GooseReceiver_removeSubscriber
functions.description: Detach a previously added GooseSubscriber from this receiver.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseReceiver and not destroyed.
subscriber must be a GooseSubscriber that was previously added to this receiver.
Must NOT be called while the receiver is running (after GooseReceiver_start) as explicitly documented.
Call before GooseReceiver_start or after GooseReceiver_stop completes.

functions.name: GooseReceiver_start
functions.description: Start the GooseReceiver in a separate thread to receive and process GOOSE messages automatically.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseReceiver and not destroyed.
Should have the desired interface set with GooseReceiver_setInterfaceId prior to starting (typical usage; not strictly stated).
Do not add or remove subscribers while running, per documentation on add/remove.
Subsequent calls when already running are unspecified (unknown).

functions.name: GooseReceiver_stop
functions.description: Stop the receiver thread previously started with GooseReceiver_start.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseReceiver and not destroyed.
Should only be called if the receiver was started via GooseReceiver_start (stopping when not started is unspecified, unknown).
After stop returns, it is safe to add or remove subscribers again.

functions.name: GooseReceiver_isRunning
functions.description: Query whether the GooseReceiver is currently running in threaded mode. Useful to confirm GooseReceiver_start succeeded.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseReceiver and not destroyed.

functions.name: GooseReceiver_destroy
functions.description: Free all resources of the GooseReceiver and all installed GooseSubscribers.
requirements: self must be a GooseReceiver created by a create function; passing NULL behavior is unspecified (unknown).
Should not be called while the receiver thread is running; stop it first (implied safe practice; not explicitly stated).
After destruction, the self handle must not be used again.

functions.name: GooseReceiver_startThreadless
functions.description: Initialize the GooseReceiver for non-threaded operation and return an EthernetSocket for manual I/O integration (e.g., event loop).
requirements: self must be a valid GooseReceiver and not destroyed.
Intended for non-threaded mode; do not mix with GooseReceiver_start.
Returned EthernetSocket must be managed according to the HAL/OS semantics (details not specified here).
Call GooseReceiver_stopThreadless to deinitialize when done.

functions.name: GooseReceiver_stopThreadless
functions.description: Deinitialize non-threaded reception started by GooseReceiver_startThreadless.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseReceiver and not destroyed.
Should only be called after GooseReceiver_startThreadless.
Do not use in combination with the threaded start/stop calls.

functions.name: GooseReceiver_tick
functions.description: Poll and parse GOOSE messages if available in non-threaded mode. Call after receiving an Ethernet frame or periodically.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseReceiver and not destroyed.
Intended for non-threaded operation; typically used after GooseReceiver_startThreadless.
Returns true if a message was available and parsed; false otherwise. Handle both cases.

functions.name: GooseReceiver_handleMessage
functions.signature: void GooseReceiver_handleMessage(GooseReceiver self, uint8_t* buffer, int size);
functions.description: Directly parse a single GOOSE message from a provided Ethernet frame buffer. Alternative to GooseReceiver_tick to avoid implementing the Ethernet HAL.
requirements: self must be a valid GooseReceiver and not destroyed.
buffer must contain the complete Ethernet message to be parsed and must be readable for size bytes.
size must be the exact size in bytes of the Ethernet message contained in buffer; must be non-negative (range otherwise unspecified).
When using this function for message injection, create the receiver with GooseReceiver_createEx(NULL) as documented.
Caller is responsible for providing messages in correct format; malformed input may be rejected or ignored (behavior unspecified).

functions.name: GoosePublisher_create
functions.signature: GoosePublisher GoosePublisher_create(CommParameters* parameters, const char* interfaceID);
functions.description: Create a new GoosePublisher instance for Ethernet GOOSE that uses VLAN tags. Provide communication parameters and the Ethernet interface name (e.g., "eth0"). Returns an opaque GoosePublisher handle on success, or NULL on failure (return semantics not documented).
requirements: self is not applicable (constructor-like function)
parameters must point to a valid CommParameters structure
interfaceID must be a valid, null-terminated C string naming an existing Ethernet interface
Uses VLAN tagging by default per note

functions.name: GoosePublisher_createEx
functions.signature: GoosePublisher GoosePublisher_createEx(CommParameters* parameters, const char* interfaceID, bool useVlanTag);
functions.description: Create a new GoosePublisher instance for Ethernet GOOSE with explicit control over VLAN tag usage. Returns an opaque GoosePublisher handle on success, or NULL on failure (return semantics not documented).
requirements: parameters must point to a valid CommParameters structure
interfaceID must be a valid, null-terminated C string naming an existing Ethernet interface
useVlanTag selects whether VLAN tags are included in GOOSE frames

functions.name: GoosePublisher_createRemote
functions.description: Create a new GoosePublisher instance for R-GOOSE (remote) transport using the provided RSession and appId. Returns an opaque GoosePublisher handle on success, or NULL on failure (return semantics not documented).
requirements: session must be a valid RSession protocol instance
appId is the GOOSE APPID value to use (16-bit)

functions.name: GoosePublisher_destroy
functions.description: Release all resources held by the GoosePublisher instance. After this call, the handle must not be used.
requirements: self must be a GoosePublisher previously created by a corresponding create function
Do not use self after destruction (dangling pointer)

functions.name: GoosePublisher_publish
functions.description: Publish a GOOSE message constructed from the provided data set. This call also increments the publisher's sequence number (sqNum). Return value semantics are not documented (success/failure unknown).
requirements: self must be a valid GoosePublisher instance
dataSet must be a valid LinkedList representing the GOOSE data set to send
Calling this function increases the internal sequence number automatically

functions.name: GoosePublisher_publishAndDump
functions.signature: int GoosePublisher_publishAndDump(GoosePublisher self, LinkedList dataSet, char* msgBuf, int32_t* msgLen, int32_t bufSize);
functions.description: Publish a GOOSE message from the provided data set and copy the exact sent message bytes into msgBuf. On return, msgLen receives the length of the sent message. Return value semantics are not documented (success/failure unknown).
requirements: self must be a valid GoosePublisher instance
dataSet must be a valid LinkedList representing the GOOSE data set to send
msgBuf must be a valid, writable buffer of at least bufSize bytes
msgLen must be a valid, writable pointer to receive the message length
bufSize must be large enough to hold the entire sent message; otherwise behavior/return value is unspecified in this header
Calling this function also increases the internal sequence number (by virtue of publish behavior)

functions.name: GoosePublisher_setGoID
functions.description: Set the GoID string used by the GoosePublisher in outgoing GOOSE messages.
requirements: self must be a valid GoosePublisher instance
goID must be a valid, null-terminated C string

functions.name: GoosePublisher_setGoCbRef
functions.description: Set the GOOSE Control Block (GoCB) reference string used by the GoosePublisher.
requirements: self must be a valid GoosePublisher instance
goCbRef must be a valid, null-terminated C string

functions.name: GoosePublisher_setTimeAllowedToLive
functions.description: Set the TimeAllowedToLive field (in milliseconds) for the GOOSE messages produced by this publisher.
requirements: self must be a valid GoosePublisher instance
timeAllowedToLive is expressed in milliseconds (range and minimum/maximum not specified)

functions.name: GoosePublisher_setDataSetRef
functions.description: Set the data set reference string used by the GoosePublisher in outgoing messages.
requirements: self must be a valid GoosePublisher instance
dataSetRef must be a valid, null-terminated C string

functions.name: GoosePublisher_setConfRev
functions.description: Set the configuration revision (ConfRev) value used by the GoosePublisher.
requirements: self must be a valid GoosePublisher instance

functions.name: GoosePublisher_setSimulation
functions.description: Set or clear the simulation flag in sent GOOSE messages.
requirements: self must be a valid GoosePublisher instance

functions.name: GoosePublisher_setStNum
functions.description: Manually set the state number (stNum) to be used for the next GOOSE message. Intended primarily for testing; prefer increasing stNum via GoosePublisher_increaseStNum when data set members change.
requirements: self must be a valid GoosePublisher instance
stNum is the state number for the next message (valid range not specified)
For production use, prefer GoosePublisher_increaseStNum when data set content changes

functions.name: GoosePublisher_setSqNum
functions.description: Manually set the sequence number (sqNum) to be used for the next GOOSE message. Intended for testing; normally sqNum is increased automatically on publish.
requirements: self must be a valid GoosePublisher instance
sqNum is the sequence number for the next message (valid range not specified)

functions.name: GoosePublisher_setNeedsCommission
functions.description: Set or clear the needs commissioning (ndsCom) flag in sent GOOSE messages.
requirements: self must be a valid GoosePublisher instance

functions.name: GoosePublisher_increaseStNum
functions.description: Increase the state number (stNum) and reset the sequence number (sqNum). Should be called whenever a member of the GOOSE data set changes. Returns a 64-bit value (exact meaning/return semantics not further documented).
requirements: self must be a valid GoosePublisher instance
Intended to be called whenever the GOOSE data set content changes
Calling this resets sqNum to 0 for the next transmission

functions.name: GoosePublisher_reset
functions.description: Reset the state and sequence numbers: sets stNum to 1 and sqNum to 0 for the GoosePublisher instance.
requirements: self must be a valid GoosePublisher instance

functions.name: SVReceiver_create
functions.description: Create a new SV receiver responsible for processing Sampled Values (SV) messages on a single Ethernet interface. Use one receiver per interface.
requirements: Must be destroyed with SVReceiver_destroy to avoid leaks.
Before starting, optionally configure the interface via SVReceiver_setInterfaceId if the default interface is not desired.
Add at least one SVSubscriber via SVReceiver_addSubscriber to receive data (not strictly required by signature but typical usage).

functions.name: SVReceiver_createRemote
functions.description: Create a new receiver instance that receives SV over a remote session (R-SV).
requirements: session must be a valid, initialized RSession.
Destroy the receiver with SVReceiver_destroy when no longer needed.
Add subscribers with SVReceiver_addSubscriber to receive ASDUs.

functions.name: SVReceiver_disableDestAddrCheck
functions.description: Disable destination MAC address checking when filtering incoming SV messages; only appID will be used for identification (default behavior).
requirements: self must be a valid SVReceiver.
Call before or during operation; understand that disabling increases risk of appID collisions in multi-stream environments.

functions.name: SVReceiver_enableDestAddrCheck
functions.description: Enable destination MAC address checking in addition to appID to identify relevant SV messages. Recommended if appIDs are not unique in the system.
requirements: self must be a valid SVReceiver.

functions.name: SVReceiver_setInterfaceId
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void SVReceiver_setInterfaceId(SVReceiver self, const char* interfaceId);
functions.description: Specify the Ethernet interface identifier (e.g., "eth0" on Linux) for the receiver instead of the library default.
requirements: self must be a valid SVReceiver.
interfaceId must point to a valid, NUL-terminated string for the platform.
Must be called before SVReceiver_start.

functions.name: SVReceiver_addSubscriber
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void SVReceiver_addSubscriber(SVReceiver self, SVSubscriber subscriber);
functions.description: Attach a subscriber to the receiver so the subscriber’s listener will be invoked for matching SV messages received on the receiver’s interface.
requirements: self must be a valid SVReceiver.
subscriber must be a valid SVSubscriber created by SVSubscriber_create.
Call before SVReceiver_start or while stopped to ensure predictable behavior (recommended; exact timing rules not specified).

functions.name: SVReceiver_removeSubscriber
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void SVReceiver_removeSubscriber(SVReceiver self, SVSubscriber subscriber);
functions.description: Detach a previously added subscriber from the receiver.
requirements: self must be a valid SVReceiver.
subscriber must be a valid SVSubscriber that was added to self.

functions.name: SVReceiver_start
functions.description: Start the receiver’s background thread to listen for and parse SV messages.
requirements: self must be a valid SVReceiver.
If a non-default network interface is required, call SVReceiver_setInterfaceId before this function.
The call spawns a background thread; ensure the environment permits thread creation.
Subscribers should be added via SVReceiver_addSubscriber to receive data.

functions.name: SVReceiver_stop
functions.description: Stop the receiver’s background thread from listening for SV messages.
requirements: self must be a valid SVReceiver.
Call after SVReceiver_start to stop the background thread before destroying the receiver.

functions.name: SVReceiver_isRunning
functions.description: Query whether the receiver’s background thread is currently running.
requirements: self must be a valid SVReceiver.

functions.name: SVReceiver_destroy
functions.description: Destroy the receiver and free associated resources.
requirements: self must be a valid SVReceiver or NULL.
Stop the receiver via SVReceiver_stop (or SVReceiver_stopThreadless) prior to destruction to ensure clean shutdown (recommended; typical lifecycle).

functions.name: SVReceiver_startThreadless
functions.description: Initialize the receiver for non-threaded operation. In this mode, the application must drive processing by calling SVReceiver_tick.
requirements: self must be a valid SVReceiver.
Do not call SVReceiver_start when using threadless mode.
After starting, the caller must call SVReceiver_tick after incoming frames and periodically for housekeeping.

functions.name: SVReceiver_stopThreadless
functions.description: Stop the receiver when operating in non-threaded mode.
requirements: self must be a valid SVReceiver started with SVReceiver_startThreadless.
After stopping, SVReceiver_tick should no longer be called until restarted.

functions.name: SVReceiver_tick
functions.description: Parse available SV messages and perform periodic housekeeping when running in threadless mode. Returns true if a message was available and parsed.
requirements: self must be a valid SVReceiver initialized via SVReceiver_startThreadless.
Call after reception of Ethernet frames and periodically for housekeeping.

functions.name: SVSubscriber_create
functions.signature: LIB61850_API SVSubscriber SVSubscriber_create(const uint8_t* ethAddr, uint16_t appID);
functions.description: Create a new SV subscriber associated with a stream identified by appID and optionally a destination Ethernet address.
requirements: ethAddr may be NULL to not specify the destination address; otherwise it must point to a 6-byte MAC address.
appID is the APP-ID used to match SV messages.
Destroy with SVSubscriber_destroy when no longer needed.

functions.name: SVSubscriber_setListener
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void SVSubscriber_setListener(SVSubscriber self, SVUpdateListener listener, void* parameter);
functions.description: Install or replace the callback invoked for each ASDU received for the subscriber’s stream. If an SV message contains multiple ASDUs, the listener is called once per ASDU.
requirements: self must be a valid SVSubscriber.
listener must be a valid function pointer or NULL (NULL would effectively remove the callback; behavior if NULL is not specified).
parameter is an opaque user pointer passed through to the callback.
ASDU objects passed to the callback are only valid within the callback invocation; copy required data if needed later.

functions.name: SVSubscriber_destroy
functions.description: Destroy a subscriber and free its resources.
requirements: self must be a valid SVSubscriber or NULL.
Ensure the subscriber is removed from any receiver (via SVReceiver_removeSubscriber) or the receiver stopped before destroying (recommended; exact requirement not specified).

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getSmpCnt
functions.description: Return the SmpCnt (sample counter) value from the ASDU, incremented for each ASDU to identify the sample.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object supplied by the library to the listener.
ASDU is only valid during the SVUpdateListener callback invocation.

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getSvId
functions.description: Return the SvID string from the ASDU.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.
Returned pointer is only valid during the callback; copy if needed afterwards.

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getDatSet
functions.description: Return the DatSet string from the ASDU, if present.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.
Use SVSubscriber_ASDU_hasDatSet to check presence; returned pointer is only valid during the callback.

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getConfRev
functions.description: Return the ConfRev (configuration revision) value from the ASDU.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getSmpMod
functions.description: Return the SmpMod value from the ASDU (sampling mode), if present.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.
Check presence with SVSubscriber_ASDU_hasSmpMod before use to avoid relying on absent data.

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getSmpRate
functions.description: Return the SmpRate value (sampling rate) from the ASDU, if present.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.
Check presence with SVSubscriber_ASDU_hasSmpRate before use.

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_hasDatSet
functions.description: Return true if the DatSet value is present in the ASDU.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_hasRefrTm
functions.description: Return true if the RefrTm (reference time) value is present in the ASDU.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_hasSmpMod
functions.description: Return true if the SmpMod value is present in the ASDU.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_hasSmpRate
functions.description: Return true if the SmpRate value is present in the ASDU.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getRefrTmAsMs
functions.description: Return the RefrTm as a millisecond timestamp since epoch, or 0 if not present.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.
Use SVSubscriber_ASDU_hasRefrTm to check presence if distinguishing between 0 and absent is necessary.

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getRefrTmAsNs
functions.description: Return the RefrTm as a nanosecond-resolution timestamp since epoch, or 0 if not present.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.
Use SVSubscriber_ASDU_hasRefrTm to check presence.

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getINT8
functions.description: Read an INT8 value from the ASDU’s data payload at the given byte index.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.
index must indicate the start byte of the value within the ASDU data.
index + 1 must be <= SVSubscriber_ASDU_getDataSize(self).
ASDU is only valid during the callback; any extracted value should be copied if needed later.

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getINT16
functions.description: Read an INT16 value from the ASDU’s data payload at the given byte index.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.
index must indicate the start byte of the 2-byte value.
index + 2 must be <= SVSubscriber_ASDU_getDataSize(self).

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getINT32
functions.description: Read an INT32 value from the ASDU’s data payload at the given byte index.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.
index + 4 must be <= SVSubscriber_ASDU_getDataSize(self).

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getINT64
functions.description: Read an INT64 value from the ASDU’s data payload at the given byte index.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.
index + 8 must be <= SVSubscriber_ASDU_getDataSize(self).

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getINT8U
functions.description: Read a UINT8 (INT8U) value from the ASDU’s data payload at the given byte index.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.
index + 1 must be <= SVSubscriber_ASDU_getDataSize(self).

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getINT16U
functions.description: Read a UINT16 (INT16U) value from the ASDU’s data payload at the given byte index.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.
index + 2 must be <= SVSubscriber_ASDU_getDataSize(self).

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getINT32U
functions.description: Read a UINT32 (INT32U) value from the ASDU’s data payload at the given byte index.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.
index + 4 must be <= SVSubscriber_ASDU_getDataSize(self).

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getINT64U
functions.description: Read a UINT64 (INT64U) value from the ASDU’s data payload at the given byte index.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.
index + 8 must be <= SVSubscriber_ASDU_getDataSize(self).

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getFLOAT32
functions.description: Read a FLOAT32 value from the ASDU’s data payload at the given byte index.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.
index + 4 must be <= SVSubscriber_ASDU_getDataSize(self).

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getFLOAT64
functions.description: Read a FLOAT64 value from the ASDU’s data payload at the given byte index.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.
index + 8 must be <= SVSubscriber_ASDU_getDataSize(self).

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getTimestamp
functions.description: Read a TimeStamp value from the ASDU’s data payload at the given byte index.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.
index must point to the start of the time value as stored in the payload.
index + 8 must be <= SVSubscriber_ASDU_getDataSize(self) (per table: TimeStamp requires 8 bytes).

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getQuality
functions.description: Read a Quality value from the ASDU’s data payload at the given byte index. Quality is encoded as a 4-byte BITSTRING.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.
index + 4 must be <= SVSubscriber_ASDU_getDataSize(self).

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getDataSize
functions.description: Return the size in bytes of the ASDU’s data payload.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.

functions.name: SVSubscriber_ASDU_getSmpSynch
functions.description: Return the SmpSynch value from the ASDU, indicating clock synchronization information.
requirements: self must be a valid ASDU object.

functions.name: SVPublisher_create
functions.signature: LIB61850_API SVPublisher SVPublisher_create(CommParameters* parameters, const char* interfaceId);
functions.description: Constructs a new IEC 61850-9-2 Sampled Values (SV) publisher bound to a network interface. VLAN tagging is enabled by default with this constructor. Pass optional communication parameters (VLAN priority, VLAN ID, appId, destination MAC).
requirements: interfaceId must point to a valid, existing network interface name string.
parameters may be NULL to use library defaults; if non-NULL, the fields should be initialized appropriately (vlanPriority, vlanId, appId, dstAddress[6]).
Returned SVPublisher must be passed to SVPublisher_destroy when no longer needed.
Call SVPublisher_setupComplete before SVPublisher_publish.

functions.name: SVPublisher_createEx
functions.signature: LIB61850_API SVPublisher SVPublisher_createEx(CommParameters* parameters, const char* interfaceId, bool useVlanTag);
functions.description: Constructs a new IEC 61850-9-2 SV publisher bound to a network interface with explicit control over VLAN tagging (enable/disable).
requirements: interfaceId must point to a valid, existing network interface name string.
parameters may be NULL to use library defaults; if non-NULL, the fields should be initialized (vlanPriority, vlanId, appId, dstAddress[6]).
useVlanTag controls VLAN tagging (true enables, false disables).
Returned SVPublisher must be destroyed with SVPublisher_destroy.
Call SVPublisher_setupComplete before SVPublisher_publish.

functions.name: SVPublisher_createRemote
functions.signature: LIB61850_API SVPublisher SVPublisher_createRemote(RSession session, uint16_t appId);
functions.description: Creates an SVPublisher instance that sends over an R-SMV (remote) transport using the provided RSession and appId.
requirements: session must reference a valid, initialized RSession instance usable for R-SMV.
appId specifies the application identifier to use for the stream and should match the intended configuration.
Returned SVPublisher must be destroyed with SVPublisher_destroy.
Call SVPublisher_setupComplete before SVPublisher_publish.

functions.name: SVPublisher_addASDU
functions.signature: LIB61850_API SVPublisher_ASDU SVPublisher_addASDU(SVPublisher self, const char* svID, const char* datset, uint32_t confRev);
functions.description: Creates an ASDU (Application Service Data Unit) and attaches it to an existing SV publisher. The ASDU carries the data payload and attributes for transmission.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher created by SVPublisher_create/_createEx/_createRemote.
svID must be a valid null-terminated identifier string for the ASDU.
datset must be a valid null-terminated dataset reference string.
confRev is the configuration revision and should be incremented when the logical device configuration changes.
After adding the required fields to the ASDU, SVPublisher_setupComplete must be called before publishing.

functions.name: SVPublisher_setupComplete
functions.description: Finalizes and prepares the SVPublisher and all associated ASDUs for transmission. Must be called before publishing and after buffer layout changes (e.g., reset).
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher.
Must be called at least once before SVPublisher_publish.
Must be called again after SVPublisher_ASDU_resetBuffer or after changes that require re-preparation (e.g., adding fields).
SVPublisher_ASDU_setSmpMod and SVPublisher_ASDU_setSmpRate must be called before this function if their values need to be set.

functions.name: SVPublisher_publish
functions.description: Sends/publishes all registered ASDUs of the publisher according to current values and attributes.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher.
SVPublisher_setupComplete must have been called successfully before publishing.
Any data to be transmitted should be written to the ASDU buffers via the corresponding set functions before calling.

functions.name: SVPublisher_destroy
functions.description: Destroys an SVPublisher instance and releases associated resources. Also invalidates any ASDUs created with it.
requirements: self may be NULL (behavior unknown if allowed; typical implementations allow NULL), otherwise must be a valid SVPublisher.
Do not use the publisher or any of its ASDUs after destruction.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_resetBuffer
functions.description: Clears the ASDU’s internal data buffer, removing all elements previously added with SVPublisher_ASDU_add* functions. Requires re-setup before publishing.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU obtained from SVPublisher_addASDU.
All previously stored indices become invalid after reset.
SVPublisher_setupComplete must be called after this operation before publishing again.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_addINT8
functions.description: Reserves space for a signed 8-bit integer element in the ASDU data block and returns its byte offset index.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
Call the corresponding setter SVPublisher_ASDU_setINT8 with the returned index to write the value.
Indices are valid until buffer reset; do not reuse after SVPublisher_ASDU_resetBuffer.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_setINT8
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void SVPublisher_ASDU_setINT8(SVPublisher_ASDU self, int index, int8_t value);
functions.description: Writes a signed 8-bit integer value into the ASDU at the given byte offset previously obtained by SVPublisher_ASDU_addINT8.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
index must be an offset previously returned by SVPublisher_ASDU_addINT8 for this ASDU and within the current data block.
Value is a signed 8-bit integer.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_addINT32
functions.description: Reserves space for a signed 32-bit integer element in the ASDU data block and returns its byte offset index.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
Use the returned index with SVPublisher_ASDU_setINT32 to assign a value.
Indices become invalid after SVPublisher_ASDU_resetBuffer.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_setINT32
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void SVPublisher_ASDU_setINT32(SVPublisher_ASDU self, int index, int32_t value);
functions.description: Writes a signed 32-bit integer value into the ASDU at the given byte offset previously obtained by SVPublisher_ASDU_addINT32.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
index must match an index returned by SVPublisher_ASDU_addINT32 for this ASDU and be within bounds.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_addINT64
functions.description: Reserves space for a signed 64-bit integer element in the ASDU data block and returns its byte offset index.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
Use the returned index with SVPublisher_ASDU_setINT64.
Indices are invalidated by SVPublisher_ASDU_resetBuffer.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_setINT64
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void SVPublisher_ASDU_setINT64(SVPublisher_ASDU self, int index, int64_t value);
functions.description: Writes a signed 64-bit integer value into the ASDU at the given byte offset previously obtained by SVPublisher_ASDU_addINT64.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
index must match an index returned by SVPublisher_ASDU_addINT64 for this ASDU and be within bounds.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_addFLOAT
functions.description: Reserves space for a single-precision (float) element in the ASDU data block and returns its byte offset index.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
Use the returned index with SVPublisher_ASDU_setFLOAT to assign a value.
Indices are invalidated by SVPublisher_ASDU_resetBuffer.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_setFLOAT
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void SVPublisher_ASDU_setFLOAT(SVPublisher_ASDU self, int index, float value);
functions.description: Writes a single-precision float value into the ASDU at the byte offset previously obtained by SVPublisher_ASDU_addFLOAT.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
index must be an offset returned by SVPublisher_ASDU_addFLOAT for this ASDU and within bounds.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_addFLOAT64
functions.description: Reserves space for a double-precision (double) element in the ASDU data block and returns its byte offset index.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
Use the returned index with SVPublisher_ASDU_setFLOAT64.
Indices are invalidated by SVPublisher_ASDU_resetBuffer.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_setFLOAT64
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void SVPublisher_ASDU_setFLOAT64(SVPublisher_ASDU self, int index, double value);
functions.description: Writes a double-precision value into the ASDU at the byte offset previously obtained by SVPublisher_ASDU_addFLOAT64.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
index must be an offset returned by SVPublisher_ASDU_addFLOAT64 for this ASDU and within bounds.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_addTimestamp
functions.description: Reserves space for a 64-bit timestamp element in the ASDU data block and returns its byte offset index.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
Use the returned index with SVPublisher_ASDU_setTimestamp to assign a value.
Timestamp type is defined elsewhere (library typedef).
Indices are invalidated by SVPublisher_ASDU_resetBuffer.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_setTimestamp
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void SVPublisher_ASDU_setTimestamp(SVPublisher_ASDU self, int index, Timestamp value);
functions.description: Writes a 64-bit timestamp value into the ASDU at the byte offset previously obtained by SVPublisher_ASDU_addTimestamp.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
index must be an offset returned by SVPublisher_ASDU_addTimestamp for this ASDU and within bounds.
Timestamp must be properly initialized per library definition.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_addQuality
functions.description: Reserves space for a quality attribute encoded as a 4-byte BIT STRING and returns its byte offset index.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
Use the returned index with SVPublisher_ASDU_setQuality to assign a value.
Indices are invalidated by SVPublisher_ASDU_resetBuffer.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_setQuality
functions.signature: LIB61850_API void SVPublisher_ASDU_setQuality(SVPublisher_ASDU self, int index, Quality value);
functions.description: Writes a quality attribute into the ASDU at the byte offset previously obtained by SVPublisher_ASDU_addQuality.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
index must be an offset returned by SVPublisher_ASDU_addQuality for this ASDU and within bounds.
Quality must be constructed per library definition (4-byte bitstring).

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_setSmpCnt
functions.description: Sets the SmpCnt (sample count) attribute of the ASDU to the specified value.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
value is a 16-bit counter value per application requirements.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_getSmpCnt
functions.description: Returns the current SmpCnt (sample count) value of the ASDU.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_increaseSmpCnt
functions.description: Increments the ASDU’s sample counter (SmpCnt) to reflect a new sample acquisition, preserving ordering; may be reset by external sync.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
Callers should reset the counter on external synchronization events if required by their application.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_setSmpCntWrap
functions.description: Sets a wrap (roll-over) limit for SmpCnt. When the counter reaches this limit, it resets to 0. Default is no limit.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
value specifies the roll-over limit; 0 implies default behavior (no limit).

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_enableRefrTm
functions.description: Enables transmission of the RefrTm (refresh time) attribute for the ASDU, which marks when data was inserted into the buffer.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
Should be called before publishing to include RefrTm in outgoing ASDUs.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_setRefrTmNs
functions.description: Sets the ASDU’s refresh time attribute with nanosecond resolution since epoch.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
refrTmNs must be a valid nanoseconds-since-epoch value as defined by the library.
If RefrTm transmission is desired, ensure SVPublisher_ASDU_enableRefrTm has been called.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_setRefrTm
functions.description: Sets the ASDU’s refresh time attribute with millisecond resolution since epoch.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
refrTm must be a valid milliseconds-since-epoch value as defined by the library.
If RefrTm transmission is desired, ensure SVPublisher_ASDU_enableRefrTm has been called.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_setRefrTmByTimestamp
functions.description: Sets the ASDU’s refresh time attribute using a Timestamp object, allowing control over time quality flags and sub-second precision (valid bits).
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
refrTm must be a valid, initialized Timestamp pointer; must not be NULL.
If RefrTm transmission is desired, ensure SVPublisher_ASDU_enableRefrTm has been called.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_setSmpMod
functions.description: Sets the sampling mode (SmpMod) of the ASDU to define interpretation of SmpRate (per nominal period, per second, or seconds per sample).
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
smpMod must be one of IEC61850_SV_SMPMOD_PER_NOMINAL_PERIOD, IEC61850_SV_SMPMOD_SAMPLES_PER_SECOND, or IEC61850_SV_SMPMOD_SECONDS_PER_SAMPLE.
Must be called before SVPublisher_setupComplete.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_setSmpRate
functions.description: Sets the sampling rate (SmpRate) for the ASDU. The unit/meaning depends on SmpMod.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
smpRate must be set consistently with the previously selected SmpMod.
Must be called before SVPublisher_setupComplete.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_setSmpSynch
functions.description: Sets the clock synchronization state (SmpSynch) for the ASDU, indicating the source/quality of time synchronization.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.

smpSynch should use allowed values: 0 (not synchronized), 1 (unspecified local clock), 2 (global clock traceable), 5–254 (local clock identified by value). Values 3, 4, and 255 are reserved and must not be used.

functions.name: SVPublisher_ASDU_setGmIdentity
functions.description: Sets the grandmaster identity (gmIdentity) for time synchronization as an 8-byte octet string on the ASDU.
requirements: self must be a valid SVPublisher_ASDU.
gmIdentity must point to a buffer of exactly 8 bytes.
