functions.name: RSession_create
functions.description: Create a new RSession instance that enables R-GOOSE/R-SMV support for GOOSE/SMV publisher/subscriber communication. Use this as the first step before configuring addresses, security, and starting the session.
requirements: Must be called before using any other RSession_* function that operates on an instance.
Returned RSession must be destroyed with RSession_destroy when no longer needed.

functions.name: RSession_setBufferSize
functions.description: Set the maximum buffer size for UDP session messages. Intended to size the internal buffers used by the RSession for sending/receiving.
requirements: self must be a valid RSession created by RSession_create and not yet destroyed.
bufferSize must be in the range 128 to 65535 (as documented).
Should be called before heavy I/O to ensure buffers are sized as desired.

functions.name: RSession_setSecurity
functions.signature: RSessionError RSession_setSecurity(RSession self, RSecurityAlgorithm secAlgo, RSignatureAlgorithm sigAlgo);
functions.description: Configure the encryption and signature algorithms used by this session. Note: applicable only for version 1 of the protocol. Returns R_SESSION_ERROR_OK on success.
requirements: self must be a valid RSession.
Only use when operating with protocol version 1 (as noted).
secAlgo must be a valid RSecurityAlgorithm value for the intended use.
sigAlgo must be a valid RSignatureAlgorithm value for the intended use.
Check the returned RSessionError and handle non-OK values.

functions.name: RSession_setLocalAddress
functions.signature: RSessionError RSession_setLocalAddress(RSession self, const char* localAddress, int localPort);
functions.description: Specify the local IP address and UDP port the session should use. Default port is 102 if not otherwise specified. Typically used to control the interface/port used when binding.
requirements: self must be a valid RSession.
localAddress must be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address string for a local interface.
localPort should be a valid UDP port number; default is 102 if not otherwise specified by the application.
Check and handle the returned RSessionError.

functions.name: RSession_addMulticastGroup
functions.signature: RSessionError RSession_addMulticastGroup(RSession self, const char* multicastAddress);
functions.description: Join the specified IPv4/IPv6 multicast group for this session so it can receive/send multicast traffic as needed. Returns R_SESSION_ERROR_OK on success, R_SESSION_ERROR_SET_FAILED otherwise.
requirements: self must be a valid RSession.
multicastAddress must be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 multicast address string.
Caller must check the returned RSessionError and handle failures (e.g., R_SESSION_ERROR_SET_FAILED).

functions.name: RSession_setMulticastTtl
functions.description: Set the multicast TTL (hop count) for packets sent by this session. Default TTL is 1 (not routable beyond local subnet).
requirements: self must be a valid RSession.
ttl is the desired multicast hop count; default is 1 as noted by documentation.
Caller must check and handle the returned RSessionError.

functions.name: RSession_setRemoteAddress
functions.signature: RSessionError RSession_setRemoteAddress(RSession self, const char* remoteAddress, int remotePort);
functions.description: Set the destination (remote) IP address and UDP port used by publishers (outgoing traffic). Returns R_SESSION_ERROR_OK on success, error code otherwise.
requirements: self must be a valid RSession.
remoteAddress must be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address string.
remotePort must be a valid UDP port number for the destination.
Caller must check and handle the returned RSessionError.

functions.name: RSession_start
functions.description: Start sending and receiving messages. This binds the session to the configured local UDP port/interface and activates communication.
requirements: self must be a valid RSession.
Must be called before attempting to send/receive via the session.
Caller must check and handle the returned RSessionError.

functions.name: RSession_stop
functions.description: Stop sending and receiving messages and release the associated socket resources for the session.
requirements: self must be a valid RSession.
Caller must check and handle the returned RSessionError.
Should be called before destroying the session or reconfiguring binding-related settings.

functions.name: RSession_addKey
functions.signature: RSessionError RSession_addKey(RSession self, uint32_t keyId, uint8_t* key, int keyLength, RSecurityAlgorithm secAlgo, RSignatureAlgorithm sigAlgo);
functions.description: Manually add a security key (and its algorithms) to the session’s accepted keys. The keyId identifies the security association. Returns an RSessionError indicating the result.
requirements: self must be a valid RSession.
keyId must be unique within the session’s key set (as implied by 'unique for the security association').
key must point to at least keyLength bytes of key data; the buffer must remain valid for the duration required by the implementation.
keyLength must be the size of the key in bytes and match the algorithms’ expected key sizes (details not documented here).
secAlgo must be an RSecurityAlgorithm applicable to the key.
sigAlgo must be an RSignatureAlgorithm applicable to the key.
Caller must check and handle the returned RSessionError (e.g., R_SESSION_ERROR_INVALID_KEY, R_SESSION_ERROR_KEY_QUEUE_FULL, etc.).

functions.name: RSession_removeKey
functions.description: Remove a previously added key (identified by keyId) from the session’s list of accepted keys.
requirements: self must be a valid RSession.
keyId must refer to an existing key previously added to the session (otherwise removal may fail depending on implementation).
Caller must check and handle the returned RSessionError.

functions.name: RSession_removeAllKeys
functions.description: Remove all keys from the session’s list of accepted keys. Use to clear the key set before reconfiguration or when revoking all associations.
requirements: self must be a valid RSession.

functions.name: RSession_setKeyEventHandler
functions.signature: void RSession_setKeyEventHandler(RSession self, RSession_KeyEventHandler handler, void* parameter);
functions.description: Register a callback to receive key-related events from the session (e.g., NEED_KEY when there is no valid key for received messages or for publishing). The user-provided parameter is passed to the callback on invocation.
requirements: self must be a valid RSession.
handler must be a valid function pointer of type RSession_KeyEventHandler (void* parameter, RSession rSession, RSessionKeyEvent event, uint32_t keyID).
The provided parameter pointer must remain valid for the lifetime of the registration or until changed by another call.

functions.name: RSession_setActiveKey
functions.description: Select the active key (by keyId) for the sender/publisher. The key must have been previously added with RSession_addKey. Returns R_SESSION_ERROR_INVALID_KEY if no valid key with the given keyId is available; otherwise R_SESSION_ERROR_OK.
requirements: self must be a valid RSession.
keyId must identify a key that has been successfully added via RSession_addKey and is currently valid.
Caller must check and handle the returned RSessionError (specifically R_SESSION_ERROR_INVALID_KEY).

functions.name: RSession_destroy
functions.description: Destroy the RSession instance and free all resources. After this call, the RSession handle must not be used.
requirements: self must be a valid RSession (non-NULL) that has not already been destroyed.
It is recommended to call RSession_stop before destroying if the session is running (implied by typical lifecycle; explicit behavior not detailed).
Do not use the RSession instance after this call.

functions.name: LogStorage_setMaxLogEntries
functions.description: Set the maximum number of log entries that the given LogStorage may keep. Typically used to cap storage growth; implementations may evict oldest entries once the cap is reached.
requirements: self must be a valid, initialized LogStorage handle.
maxEntries is a count of entries; it should be a non-negative integer (inferred from purpose as a maximum count).

functions.name: SqliteLogStorage_createInstance
functions.description: Create a new LogStorage instance backed by an embedded SQLite database. Use this when the library is compiled with SQLite support to persist log entries to the file given by filename.
requirements: Library must be compiled with SQLite support for this function to be available (explicit note).
filename should be a valid null-terminated path string to the SQLite database file (inferred from parameter name and description).
Caller is responsible for destroying the returned LogStorage with LogStorage_destroy when no longer needed.

functions.name: LogStorage_getMaxLogEntries
functions.description: Return the maximum allowed number of log entries configured for the given LogStorage.
requirements: self must be a valid, initialized LogStorage handle.

functions.name: LogStorage_addEntry
functions.description: Create a new log entry with the given entry time (milliseconds timestamp) and return its entryID. Use this before adding one or more data items to the entry with LogStorage_addEntryData.
requirements: self must be a valid, initialized LogStorage handle.
timestamp is an entry time in milliseconds (explicit in comment); it should represent the intended event time (inferred).

functions.name: LogStorage_addEntryData
functions.signature: bool LogStorage_addEntryData(LogStorage self, uint64_t entryID, const char* dataRef, uint8_t* data, int dataSize, uint8_t reasonCode);
functions.description: Attach a data item to an existing log entry identified by entryID. The data is an unstructured binary blob with an associated data reference and reason code.
requirements: self must be a valid, initialized LogStorage handle.
entryID must refer to an existing log entry previously created with LogStorage_addEntry (explicit from description).
dataRef must be a valid null-terminated string denoting the data reference (inferred from const char* usage).
data must point to a buffer of at least dataSize bytes; dataSize specifies the number of bytes to read (inferred from typical C API and parameter description).
dataSize must be >= 0 (inferred from being a size/count).
reasonCode is an 8-bit value; valid meanings depend on the application and are not specified here (unknown details).

functions.name: LogStorage_getEntries
functions.signature: bool LogStorage_getEntries(LogStorage self, uint64_t startingTime, uint64_t endingTime, LogEntryCallback entryCallback, LogEntryDataCallback entryDataCallback, void* parameter);
functions.description: Iterate over log entries in the inclusive time range [startingTime, endingTime]. For each entry, the implementation calls entryCallback for the entry metadata and entryDataCallback for each associated data item, passing the user-supplied parameter. Callbacks can return false to abort retrieval. The moreFollow flag indicates whether more data is expected; when false, the current data is not valid and no further data follows for that sequence.
requirements: self must be a valid, initialized LogStorage handle.
startingTime and endingTime are timestamps in milliseconds (inferred from API consistency).
entryCallback must be a valid function pointer conforming to LogEntryCallback and should tolerate being called zero or more times.
entryDataCallback must be a valid function pointer conforming to LogEntryDataCallback and should tolerate being called zero or more times per entry.
The callbacks must be prepared to handle moreFollow=false, which indicates the provided data is not valid and no more data will follow (explicit in callback docs).
The callbacks should return true to continue receiving data; returning false aborts the operation (explicit in callback docs).
parameter is an opaque pointer passed unchanged to the callbacks; if non-NULL, it must remain valid for the duration of the call (inferred).

functions.name: LogStorage_getEntriesAfter
functions.signature: bool LogStorage_getEntriesAfter(LogStorage self, uint64_t startingTime, uint64_t entryID, LogEntryCallback entryCallback, LogEntryDataCallback entryDataCallback, void* parameter);
functions.description: Iterate over all log entries that were added after the specified starting log entry (identified by startingTime and entryID). For each entry found, the implementation invokes entryCallback and entryDataCallback, passing the user parameter. Callbacks can return false to abort. The moreFollow flag semantics are the same as in getEntries.
requirements: self must be a valid, initialized LogStorage handle.
startingTime is the timestamp of the starting log entry; entryID is that entry's ID (explicit). Both together identify the starting point.
entryCallback must be a valid LogEntryCallback pointer; it may be called zero or more times until completion or abort.
entryDataCallback must be a valid LogEntryDataCallback pointer; it may be called zero or more times per entry.
Callbacks must handle moreFollow=false to mean the provided data is not valid and no more data will follow (explicit in callback docs).
Callbacks should return true to continue; returning false aborts the operation (explicit in callback docs).
parameter, if non-NULL, must remain valid for the duration of the call (inferred).

functions.name: LogStorage_getOldestAndNewestEntries
functions.signature: bool LogStorage_getOldestAndNewestEntries(LogStorage self, uint64_t* newEntry, uint64_t* newEntryTime, uint64_t* oldEntry, uint64_t* oldEntryTime);
functions.description: Retrieve the entryID and entry time of the newest and oldest entries currently stored. Intended to update log status information (e.g., in an LCB). Returns true on success.
requirements: self must be a valid, initialized LogStorage handle.
newEntry, newEntryTime, oldEntry, and oldEntryTime are output pointers that must point to writable memory (inferred from "pointer to store" phrasing).

functions.name: LogStorage_destroy
functions.description: Destroy the LogStorage instance and free all related resources. After this call, the handle must not be used.
requirements: self must be a valid LogStorage handle obtained from a compatible creator (e.g., SqliteLogStorage_createInstance) and not already destroyed.
After calling, the self handle becomes invalid and must not be used again (inferred).

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: filesystem path
# Requirements from stubs:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(): should point to an existing readable file containing random data for cases like
#   ConfigFileParser_createModelFromConfigFileEx (expects an existing file) and other file ops (open/get/set/obtain).
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR(): often used as base paths or destination filenames; not required to exist, but should be a
#   plausible, NUL-terminated path-like string.
# Strategy:
# - Provide a self-describing container that includes one or more path-like strings and an embedded file payload.
# - The harness will typically request only one parameter per call; therefore we craft a single primary path that
#   looks valid and include an extension to steer different code paths (e.g., .cfg, .bin, .txt).
# - Content will be syntactically valid text or binary to help parsers.
# - Returned buffer layout:
#   [header]\n[path]\n\0[data]\n
# Layout details:
#   header: ASCII magic "PATH\n" to aid any debug tools (harmless for fuzzer).
#   path: relative path with nested directories like a/b/c/name.ext ensuring directories are simple and safe.
#   data: file payload bytes to be written by the fuzzer runtime into the file backing FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() if it
#         mirrors this buffer; since we cannot do I/O here, we embed the payload so the runtime that provisions
#         FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME can seed from this buffer.
# Note: We keep the entire buffer <= 4096 bytes.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"
EXTS = ["cfg", "conf", "ini", "txt", "bin", "dat", "iec", "mms"]


def _rand_name(rng: random.Random, min_len=3, max_len=12) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_dirs(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # 0..3 subdirectories
    depth = rng.randint(0, 3)
    dirs = []
    for _ in range(depth):
        # Include some common directory-like names occasionally
        if rng.random() < 0.25:
            dirs.append(rng.choice(["tmp", "var", "etc", "home", "cfg", "data"]))
        else:
            dirs.append(_rand_name(rng))
    return dirs


def _rand_extension(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Bias to text-like for config parser; sometimes binary
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return rng.choice(EXTS[:-2])  # prefer text-ish
    return rng.choice(EXTS)


def _rand_rel_or_abs(rng: random.Random) -> bool:
    # Absolute paths sometimes; relative more common and safer for sandboxes
    return rng.random() < 0.3


def _build_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = _rand_dirs(rng)
    base = _rand_name(rng)
    ext = _rand_extension(rng)
    filename = f"{base}.{ext}"
    sep = os.sep
    path = sep.join(parts + [filename]) if parts else filename
    if _rand_rel_or_abs(rng):
        # Create an absolute-style path without relying on the real FS root
        root = sep
        # optionally add a root directory hint
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            path = sep.join([rng.choice(["tmp", "var", "etc", "home", "config", "mnt"]) , path])
        path = root + path if not path.startswith(root) else path
    else:
        # occasionally prefix with . or .. for relative
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            prefix = rng.choice([".", "..", os.path.join("..", "..")])
            path = os.path.join(prefix, path)
    # Cap length to something reasonable for stubs that trim to 256
    if len(path) > 240:
        path = path[:240]
    return path


def _gen_text_payload(rng: random.Random, target_ext: str) -> bytes:
    # Create plausible configuration/text formats based on extension to increase parseability
    lines = []
    if target_ext in ("cfg", "conf"):
        # INI-like and key=value pairs
        sections = ["General", "Server", "Model", "Paths"]
        for sec in sections[: rng.randint(1, len(sections))]:
            lines.append(f"[{sec}]\n")
            kv_count = rng.randint(2, 8)
            for _ in range(kv_count):
                k = _rand_name(rng, 3, 10)
                # some values as numbers, some as paths
                if rng.random() < 0.4:
                    v = str(rng.randint(0, 100000))
                elif rng.random() < 0.3:
                    v = _build_path(rng)
                else:
                    v = _rand_name(rng, 3, 20)
                lines.append(f"{k}={v}\n")
            lines.append("\n")
    elif target_ext in ("ini", "txt"):
        # Simple lines with comments
        for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 40)):
            if rng.random() < 0.2:
                lines.append("# comment\n")
            else:
                k = _rand_name(rng, 3, 12)
                v = _rand_name(rng, 1, 24)
                lines.append(f"{k} {v}\n")
    else:
        # For others, return empty to let binary payload handle
        return b""
    data = ''.join(lines).encode('utf-8')
    # limit size
    if len(data) > 3000:
        data = data[:3000]
    return data


def _gen_binary_payload(rng: random.Random, min_size=32, max_size=2048) -> bytes:
    size = rng.randint(min_size, max_size)
    b = bytearray(size)
    # Fill with a mix of distributions to create structure-like patterns
    i = 0
    while i < size:
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.2 and i + 8 <= size:
            # put a little-endian uint64 timestamp-like
            val = rng.getrandbits(64)
            b[i:i+8] = val.to_bytes(8, 'little')
            i += 8
        elif choice < 0.5 and i + 4 <= size:
            # 32-bit word
            val = rng.getrandbits(32)
            b[i:i+4] = val.to_bytes(4, 'little')
            i += 4
        else:
            b[i] = rng.randrange(0, 256)
            i += 1
    return bytes(b)


def _compose_buffer(path: str, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Compose buffer: magic + path + NUL + payload
    magic = b"PATH\n"
    path_bytes = path.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    # Ensure NUL-terminated semantics by including a NUL separator
    out = magic + path_bytes + b"\x00" + payload
    # Cap total length
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096]
    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a plausible file path
    path = _build_path(rng)
    ext = os.path.splitext(path)[1].lstrip('.').lower()

    # Generate payload: prefer text for text-like extensions; otherwise binary
    text_payload = _gen_text_payload(rng, ext)
    if text_payload:
        # Optionally append some binary tail to exercise mixed readers
        if rng.random() < 0.25:
            tail = _gen_binary_payload(rng, 8, 128)
            payload = text_payload + tail
        else:
            payload = text_payload
    else:
        payload = _gen_binary_payload(rng)

    # Compose and return
    return _compose_buffer(path, payload)
